entries.description: (gauge, mount, name, row, cockpit, block) in stack order, callee-cleaned (RET 0x18): allocates 0xb8 bytes with Mem_New (000015a4) when gauge is null, returning 0 when that fails; WeaponGauge_Ctor (00036f50)(gauge, mount, cockpit, block); WeaponGaugeVtable (00093a6e) at +0x76, the int16 row at +0xa2, the inlined constructor of the rect +0xa8, ProjectileWeaponGaugeVtable (00093aae) at +0x76. With (x, y) the block's first two dwords: child 0 = ChainedWeaponSelectGadget_Ctor (00038338)(0, row, gauge, the block's rect +0x10 moved by (x, y)) at +0x14, registered with Widget_RegisterClickable (000443d4) in the root widget of CockpitViewInstance (00092d1c); strncpy (0006745c)(+0x7a, name, 0xc); +0xa8..+0xb4 = the block's rect +0x20 moved by (x, y); the label Label_Ctor (00030f44)(0, ColorSchemePanels[3] at 00092d4c) at +0xa4, placed by Label_SetRect (00031080)(label, 1, +0xa8, zero margins), its fill +0x1c = 0x3f; +0x64 = 1; memset (00060b40)(+0x8b, 0, 0x17). Returns gauge. ES2's AmmoWeaponGauge_Ctor (DBSIM 00440f78).

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_Paint
entries.description: (gauge) in stack order, callee-cleaned (RET 4): slot +8 of ProjectileWeaponGaugeVtable (00093aae). Calls slot +4 of child +0x14's table; then, when CockpitView_RectCornerVisible (0002b214)(the label +0xa4's rect +4) passes, child +0x14's int16 +0x17 is not 2 and +0x9c is clear: installs the brush {0, 0x3f} at the render context's (000bdbda) +0x22c, Raster_FillRect (00053d9c)(+0xa8), ltoa (00064720)(+0x8b, an 8-byte buffer, 10) and Label_SetText (0003114c)(label, buffer). ES2's AmmoWeaponGauge_Paint (DBSIM 004411b4).

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_Update
entries.description: (gauge) in stack order, callee-cleaned: slot +0xc of ProjectileWeaponGaugeVtable (00093aae). Calls slot +0x10 of child +0x14's table. With the byte +0x75 at 2 and CockpitView_RectCornerVisible (0002b214)(the label +0xa4's rect +4) passing: unless +0x9c is set, fills +0xa8 with the brush {0, 0x3f} (Raster_FillRect (00053d9c)) and writes ltoa (00064720)(+0x8b) into the label (Label_SetText (0003114c)); then lowers +0x75. The lowering at 2 is inside the visibility test, so a label off screen keeps +0x75 at 2. With +0x75 at 1: unless +0x9c is set, Widget_DrawToCockpit (0002b058)(0, the label's rect, 0); then lowers +0x75. ES2's AmmoWeaponGauge_Update (DBSIM 00441268).

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_SetState
entries.description: (gauge, block) in stack order, callee-cleaned: slot +0x14 of ProjectileWeaponGaugeVtable (00093aae). A block +0 that differs from +0x8b goes there and sets +0x75 to 2; a byte +0x11 that differs from +0x9c goes there and sets child +0x14's int16 +0x17 to 2 (set) or 0; the bytes +0x14..+0x16 go to +0x9f..+0xa1 when they differ; when any byte changed it calls slot +8 of child +0x14's table. ES2's AmmoWeaponGauge_SetState (DBSIM 004413f4), which also sets its repaint counter on a byte change.

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_GetState
entries.description: Frameless: (gauge), callee-cleaned (RET 4): returns gauge + 0x8b, the 0x17-byte state block. ES2's AmmoWeaponGauge_GetState (DBSIM 004414a4). es2_xref finds one call, from WeaponMount_PushAmmoGaugeState (0000b67c).

entries.name: AmmoWeaponGauge_OnChildClick
entries.description: (gauge, value, child) in stack order, callee-cleaned: slot +4 of ProjectileWeaponGaugeVtable (00093aae). Finds the child among the +0x64 children from +0x14; for child 0, with bit 1 of value set, WeaponMounts_ToggleChainMember (0000d5e4)(the weapon manager +0x198 of CockpitViewInstance (00092d1c)'s machine +0x1ff, the dword at +0xa2), otherwise CockpitView_ArmWeaponByGauge (0002d098)(+0x10, gauge). ES2's AmmoWeaponGauge_OnChildClick (DBSIM 004414b4), which also sets its repaint counter.

entries.name: PodGauge_Ctor
entries.description: (gauge, mount, row, cockpit, block) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: the ECM's pod row. Allocates 0xa1 bytes when given none (0 on failure), runs WeaponGauge_Ctor (00036f50)(gauge, mount, cockpit, block) and stores PodGaugeVtable (00093ace) at +0x76. With (x, y) the block's top-left: child 0 = WeaponSelectGadget_Ctor (000380fc)(0, row, gauge, the block's rect at +0x10 moved by (x, y)) at +0x14, registered with Widget_RegisterClickable on CockpitViewInstance's root widget; strncpy of 12 bytes of STRINGS0.STR group 3's string (000bd2c8, ECM) to +0x7a; the label rect +0x91 = the block's rect at +0x20 moved by (x, y), the label Label_Ctor(0, cpred 00092d48) at +0x8d placed by Label_SetRect(label, 2, rect, {0, 0}) with fill 0x3f; child count +0x64 = 1; memset(+0x8b, 0, 2), the switch and the destroyed byte. Returns the gauge. ES2's PodGauge_Ctor (DBSIM 00441524) with TogglePodGauge_Ctor (DBSIM 00441998), which build the name from the mount and place the label at fixed offsets.

entries.name: PodGauge_Paint
entries.description: (gauge), its argument removed by this function; slot +8 of PodGaugeVtable (00093ace). Calls child 0's paint (slot +4 of the table at its +0x1c); then, when CockpitView_RectCornerVisible passes the label's rect and child 0's int16 state +0x17 is not 2, installs a stack brush at the render context's +0x22c and writes the label with Label_SetText in cpylw (00092d4c): with the destroyed byte +0x8c clear, the name +0x7a on fill 0x38 while the switch +0x8b is set and 0x3f while it is clear; with it set, OFFLINE (000bd2c4) on 0x3f, the label placed again by Label_SetRect(label, 2, {child 0's x0, y0, the label's x1, y1}, {0, 0}), and child 0's state set to 2. ES2's PodGauge_Paint (DBSIM 0044171c), which also gates on armed, dark and mid-wipe.

entries.name: PodGauge_Update
entries.description: (gauge), its argument removed by this function; slot +0xc of PodGaugeVtable (00093ace). Steps the repaint counter +0x75: at 2 the paint (slot +8 of the table at +0x76), at 1 Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, the label's rect, 0), each lowering it by 1; at 0 child 0's per-frame slot +0x10. ES2's PodGauge_Update (DBSIM 00441850) without its gates, power-up and sensor dropout.

entries.name: PodGauge_SetStateBlock
entries.description: (gauge, block), its arguments removed by this function: when the block's byte 0 or byte 1 differs from the gauge's +0x8b or +0x8c, copies the two bytes to +0x8b and sets the repaint counter +0x75 to 2. es2_xref finds one call, from CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand (0002d24c). ES2's TogglePodGauge_SetStateBlock (DBSIM 004419c4), which also copies the next dword.

entries.name: PodGauge_GetStateBlock
entries.description: Frameless: MOV EAX,[ESP+4], ADD EAX,0x8b, RET 4: (gauge) returns gauge + 0x8b, the pod row's state block (byte 0 the switch, byte 1 the destroyed byte). es2_xref finds calls from CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand (0002d24c) and EcmMount_PushGaugeState (0000b588). ES2's PodGauge_GetStateBlock (DBSIM 00441978).

entries.name: PodGauge_OnChildClick
entries.description: (gauge, value, child) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function; slot +4 of PodGaugeVtable (00093ace): when the child is child 0 (+0x14, among +0x64 children), flips byte 0 of +0x8b, the switch, and sets the repaint counter +0x75 to 2, whatever the value. ES2's TogglePodGauge_OnClick (DBSIM 004419fc).

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_Ctor
entries.description: (console, cockpit, block) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: allocates 0x7e bytes when given none (0 on failure), runs PanelGauge_Ctor (00031318)(console, cockpit, block) and stores WeaponRangeGaugeVtable (00093aee) at +0x76. With (x, y) the block's first two int32, for i 0 to 4: the block's rect at +0x10 + 16i moved by (x, y); WeaponRangeSelectGadget_Ctor (00038ce4)(0, console, rect), registered with Widget_RegisterClickable on CockpitViewInstance's root widget and stored at +0x14 + 4i; a label Label_Ctor(0, cpgreen 00092d44) placed by Label_SetRect(label, 2, rect, {0, 0}) at the button's +0x2c, and i at its +0x28. Count +0x64 = 5, +0x7c = 0; it writes neither +0x7a nor +0x7d. The buttons are I, II, III, LINK and TRACK. ES2's ConsoleButtons_Ctor (DBSIM 00441dd0) builds four.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_SetChainNumber
entries.description: (console, chain), its arguments removed by this function: stores the int16 chain at +0x7a; for 0, 1 or 2 sets that chain button's lamp byte +0x3c (+0x14, +0x18 or +0x1c) to 1 and the other two's to 0, repainting (slot +8 of the button's table at +0x1c) only a button whose lamp changes. es2_xref finds calls from Gau_WeaponButtonsWidget (0002ccd8), WeaponMounts_SetChain (0000cf10), ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock (00037e78) and, twice, ConsoleButtons_HandleCommand (00038034). ES2's ConsoleButtons_SetChainNumber (DBSIM 00441f68), which stores the number alone.

entries.description: (console), its argument removed by this function: flips the tracking latch byte +0x7c. ES2's ConsoleButtons_ToggleAutoTrack (DBSIM 00441f7c), which also refuses a state-2 TRACK button, copies the latch to its lamp, repaints it and posts the AUTO TRACKING messages.

entries.description: (console, value), its arguments removed by this function: stores the byte value at +0x7d, the link request. ES2's ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch (DBSIM 0044202c), which also runs WeaponMounts_ToggleLink.

entries.description: (console), its argument removed by this function; slot +8 of WeaponRangeGaugeVtable (00093aee): calls slot +4, the paint, of each of the five buttons at +0x14 (each's table at its +0x1c). ES2's ConsoleButtons_Paint (DBSIM 00442058), over four.

entries.description: (console), its argument removed by this function; slot +0xc of WeaponRangeGaugeVtable (00093aee): calls slot +0x10, the per-frame flush, of each of the five buttons at +0x14. ES2's ConsoleButtons_Update (DBSIM 0044207c), over four.

entries.name: ConsoleButtons_SetStateBlock
entries.description: (console, block), its arguments removed by this function: a block int16 +0 other than +0x7a is stored there and handed to ConsoleButtons_SetChainNumber (00037ce4); a byte +2 other than +0x7c runs ConsoleButtons_ToggleAutoTrack (00037df8); a byte +3 other than +0x7d goes to ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch (00037e0c). es2_xref finds one call, from WeaponMounts_PerFrameUpdate (0000cf78). entries.name: ConsoleButtons_OnChildClick
entries.description: (console, flags, button) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function; slot +4 of WeaponRangeGaugeVtable (00093aee): finds the button's index among the +0x64 at +0x14. For 0, 1 or 2 it puts out the other two chain buttons' lamps +0x3c, repainting (slot +8) each that was lit, and stores the index at +0x7a; for 3 (LINK) ConsoleButtons_SetLinkLatch (00037e0c)(console, 1); for 4 (TRACK) ConsoleButtons_ToggleAutoTrack (00037df8). PanelGauge_Ctor (00031318); the three comm-box gauges at +0xf6 (0x14a bytes, CommBox_ElementCtor (0003cab8)); HDDGaugeVtable (0009451e) at +0x76; the clip context CommBox_ClipContext (000b15f8) from GLViewport_Ctor; dba\static into HddStaticBank (000944d0) the first time; the screen rect +0x8a, damage column +0x9a, order column +0xaa from int32 4-7, 12-15, 8-11 plus the origin int32 0-1; +0xd2 = -1; the pages HddCommandScreen_Ctor (0003ee58)(0, display, order column, screen) at +0xca and HddDamageScreen_Ctor (00042164)(0, display, damage column, screen) at +0xce; the fifteen buttons HddButton_Ctor (0003ea5c)(0, i, display, int32 0x14+4i.. plus origin) at +0x14 + 4i with dba\pbuttons frames (22-25, the arrows from int32 0x5c with Widget_SetHitShape (00043784)(button, 1) when that is 0x23, 51-54), each registered with Widget_RegisterClickable on the cockpit's root; XMIT's, CANCEL's and the title's (+0x4d8, on button 9's rect) labels in cpred, centered, fill 0x3f; +0x64 = 15; the title indicator +0xba from int32 16-19; each gauge's marker rect +0x2d from int32 0x50+4i and name +0x137 = 0; +0x4e8 = +0x4d4 = -1; HddDisplay_SetPage(display, 0); CommBox_OnMessageBegin and CommBox_OnMessageEnd added to CockpitView_GetSquadMessagePort's port; HddDisplayInstance (000944cc) = display; +0x4e5 = 0xff; the highlight mode +0x4e6 from int32 0x5e; str\pilots into HddPilotNameTable (000944d4) the first time; the five subjects and names (YOU, three empty, TARGET), +0x4dc = 1, +0x51b = NO TARGET SELECTED. ES2's HddDisplay_Ctor (DBSIM 00448cc8).

entries.name: CommBox_ElementCtor
entries.description: (gauge) callee-cleaned: one comm-box gauge's element constructor for __vec_ctor: allocates 0x14a bytes when given none, returning 0 when that fails, runs the inlined rect constructors of +0x1d and +0x2d and __vec_ctor over the 30 eight-byte offset pairs at +0x3d with Point_DefaultCtorHddCopy (0003cb74) by its padding. ES2's CommBox_ElementCtor (DBSIM 0044c0e7).

entries.name: Point_DefaultCtorHddCopy
entries.description: (p) callee-cleaned: allocates 8 bytes when p is null and returns p; the element constructor of a comm-box gauge's offset pairs, which CommBox_ElementCtor (0003cab8) passes by its padding 0003cb71. The code of Point_DefaultCtorGunsightCopy (000345a0).

entries.name: HddDisplay_Repaint
entries.description: (display) callee-cleaned, slot +8 (paint) of HDDGaugeVtable: while CockpitView_RectCornerVisible passes the screen rect +0x8a: each button's paint slot +4, with no state test; the current page's show (+0x10) and repaint (+4) through its +0xc table; the title indicator +0xba filled 0x3b while +0x4dc is set, else 0x39; HddDisplay_SetTitle; for each comm box, button 10+i's rect copied into the gauge's +0x1d and inset there by one pixel, filled 0x3f when the gauge's name +0x137 is 0, else HddGauge_PaintIdle. ES2's HddDisplay_Repaint (DBSIM 00449a50).

entries.name: HddDisplay_Update
entries.description: (display) callee-cleaned, slot +0xc (per frame) of HDDGaugeVtable: the cockpit's selection +0x20c as subject slot 4 (+0x501), with +0x51b NO TARGET SELECTED when null and NO INFO AVAILABLE (and the subject null) for a class +0x162 other than 0; on a change, the subject +0x4e1 when the selector is 4, HddDisplay_LastTarget (0009456c) and page 1's update flag +0xd9; HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress; comms-out latches (gauge +0x147) for destroyed (+0x93) squadmates on a frame the view manager's +0x18 is set in view 4, and state 1 for every destroyed and latched box; HddDisplay_ServiceCommBoxes; outside view 4 the sensor dropout on Player_DependentCondition(4) (PanelGauge_TickDropout), a full repaint of the page when +0x74 changes, and while the screen rect is visible each button's slot +0x10, page 1's half-second refresh (+0x4ed, 0x1e counts) and the two-frame paint stages on +0x75 through the page's +4 and +8 slots, the copy of stage 1 lifting the pilot channel's line (its slots +0x14 and +0x18) while one is up, the GL display 000bdd28's draw page +0x3c set to its +0x88 first and left there. ES2's HddDisplay_Update (DBSIM 00449bd0), with RepaintPage and PaintCurrentScreen inlined.

entries.name: HddDisplay_NoOp
entries.description: Frameless: RET 8, between HddDisplay_Update and HddDisplay_KeyDispatch, where ES2's HddDisplay_NoOp (DBSIM 00449fbc) stands. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: HddDisplay_ReturnZero
entries.description: Frameless: XOR EAX,EAX and RET 4: returns 0. Between HddDisplay_Update and HddDisplay_KeyDispatch, where ES2's HddDisplay_ReturnZero (DBSIM 00449fc4) stands. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: HddDisplay_KeyDispatch
entries.description: (display, code) in stack order, callee-cleaned, slot +0x10 (key) of HDDGaugeVtable: REPNE SCASD over the 17 codes of HddDisplay_KeyCodes (00094574), jumping through the 17 dwords after them; any other code goes to the current page's key slot (+0x14 of its +0xc table), whose answer it returns, and a listed one returns 1. Arrows 0x48/0x50/0x4b/0x4d press buttons 2-5, 0x02-0x04 buttons 10-12, 0x0c/0x4a button 6, 0x0d/0x4e button 7 (a press skips state 2 and 3 and calls the click slot with (button, 1)); 0x1f/0x17/0x11 run HddDisplay_SetPage(display, 1) and HddDamageScreen_SetView (000423d8)(damage screen, 0/1/2); 0x64b, 0x64d and 0x62b (Ctrl+Alt with keypad 4, keypad 6, backslash) step HddDebugMessageId (00094570) down to 0, up to 0x29, or leave it, after making a negative one 1, and post {that id, g_SquadmateMachines[0]} to the pilot channel with MessagePort_Post. ES2's HddDisplay_KeyDispatch (DBSIM 00449fcc), which has none of the three Ctrl+Alt codes.
entries.source: Herculan/docs/es1/simulation/heads-down-display.md#keys; ES1DBSIM decompile at 0003d12c, after ES2RepairFunctionBody's switch preview

entries.name: HddDisplay_OnChildClick
entries.description: (display, value, button) in stack order, callee-cleaned, slot +4 of HDDGaugeVtable: stores the button's index among the +0x64 buttons from +0x14 in the byte +0x4e5. ES2's HddDisplay_OnChildClick (DBSIM 0044a14c).

entries.name: HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress
entries.description: (display) callee-cleaned: switched on the pressed index +0x4e5, which it puts back to 0xff; returns at once at 0xff, and while the display is dark (+0x74) returns for a button above 1 leaving the index. 0/1 HddDisplay_SetPage; 2-7 on page 0 the command screen's HddMap_PanUp (0003fd2c), HddMap_PanDown (0003fd58), HddMap_PanLeft (0003fcd4), HddMap_PanRight (0003fd00), HddMap_ZoomOut (0003fc70), HddMap_ZoomIn (0003fca4) with page 0's update flag +0xd8 and the stage +0x75 = 2; 2/3 and 9 on page 1 the damage screen's HddDamageScreen_NextView (0004246c) or HddDamageScreen_PrevView (00042494) with +0xd7; 4/5 on page 1 HddDisplay_PrevSubject/NextSubject into +0x4e1 and the title indicator from the subject's +0x9d, a null subject as clear (0x3b set, 0x39 clear, copied with Widget_DrawToCockpit); 10-12 (page 1 switching to 0 first, nothing on another page) HddDisplay_SelectPilot for a slot not selected whose machine is set and not destroyed (+0x93), then Cockpit_SetOffForwardCursor(2) while the command screen's +0x103 is set; 13 XMIT on page 0: HddCommandScreen_SetMessageRow (00040834)(screen, 1, 0) with +0x104 clear, else HddCommandScreen_CommitPick (0004075c), and with a pilot selected the word +0x5d into HddOrderRecord (000b0ddc), HddCommandScreen_FillOrderRecord (0004070c), Squad_SendOrderToSlot(cockpit +0x10, slot, record), Cockpit_SetOffForwardCursor(0), HddCommandScreen_CancelTransmission (000407d4), HddDisplay_SelectPilot(-1); 14 CANCEL: HddCommandScreen_CancelTransmission (000407d4), Cockpit_SetOffForwardCursor(0), HddDisplay_SelectPilot(-1). ES2's HddDisplay_HandleWidgetPress (DBSIM 0044a178).

entries.name: HddDisplay_SetPage
entries.description: (display, page) in stack order, callee-cleaned: when the page differs from +0xd2, the old page's hide (slot +0xc of its +0xc table) unless +0xd2 is -1, +0xd2 = page, the new page's show (+0x10), and HddPageWidgetVisibility (000944dc) row page applied to the buttons, a 1 moving state 2 to 0 and a 0 moving state 0 to 2, each invalidated (slot +8); then, either way, the page's full-repaint flag +0xd6+page and the stage +0x75 = 2. ES2's HddDisplay_SetPage (DBSIM 0044a5e4), which also relights the page buttons.

entries.name: HddDisplay_SetTitle
entries.description: (display) callee-cleaned: Label_SetText on the title label +0x4d8 with MAP (000bd350, STRINGS0 group 10) on page 0, or entry +0x74 of the damage screen (+0xce) of 000bd358 (group 11) on page 1; nothing on another page. ES2's HddDisplay_SetTitle (DBSIM 0044a6dc).

entries.name: HddDisplay_SelectPilot
entries.description: (display, slot) in stack order, callee-cleaned: with a slot selected (+0x4d4 not -1) clears that comm box's (button 10+slot) lamp +0x3c and invalidates it when it was set; +0x4e8 = +0x4d4, +0x4d4 = slot; for a slot other than -1, sets its box's lamp and invalidates it when it was clear, and posts {0x22, g_SquadmateMachines[slot]} to CockpitView_GetSquadMessagePort's port with MessagePort_Post; last HddCommandScreen_SelectPilot (00040664)(command screen +0xca, +0x4d4). ES2's HddDisplay_SelectPilot (DBSIM 0044a720).

entries.name: HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames
entries.description:
(display, pilot, slot) in stack order, callee-cleaned: for slot 0 the pilot is CommBox0PilotOverride (000944d8) when that is not negative; the portrait p = Pilot_PortraitOf(pilot) at gauge +0x135 and the name at +0x137, entry p of HddPilotNameTable (str\pilots, by StrTable_FirstString and p StrTable_NextString); SystemMessages_Index(pilot channel, Pilot_VoiceBankOf(p), slot); ofs\pilot

through a VolRStream (assert severity 5, phdd.cpp line 0x3c1) read as 27 entries {int32 k, 8 bytes into pair k at +0x3d}; the bank dba\pilot

at +0x18 with +0x133 = 1, or dba\pilot

s and +0x133 = 0 while g_LowMemory is set (assert at line 0x3d9 when null); six labels on button 10+slot's rect (name in cpred on HudColorTable_Get(slot), then cpblue/cpred/cpblue/cpred at y0+16/24/32/40, a sixth 10x10 at the bottom-left in cpred on 0x3b); clears +0x13f, +0x13b, +0x12e, +0x147, +0x149, +0x148; subject slot 1+slot = the squadmate's machine and its name. ES2's HddGauge_LoadPilotFrames (DBSIM 0044a7c0), which walks the names to the pilot's own number.

entries.name: HddGauge_ConditionIndex
entries.description: (display, machine) in stack order, callee-cleaned: Mech_ReadDamageReadouts (0001583c) into a stack buffer of 42 int16 (84 bytes), which it fills whole; then the mean of entries 1-19 as (0x100 - mean) * 100 >> 8, bucketed at 90, 74, 51 and 1 into 0-4. ES2's HddGauge_ConditionIndex (DBSIM 0044adf4), identical after normalization but for the buffer's address argument.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintIdle
entries.description: (display, slot) in stack order, callee-cleaned: while CockpitView_RectCornerVisible passes the screen rect +0x8a: with g_SquadmateMachines[slot]'s +0x93 clear (the machine read with no null test), inside Cockpit_PushCanvasContext/PopRenderContext, fills the gauge's video rect +0x1d with 0x3f and sets the five labels: the name, STATUS: (000bd4a0), 000bd46c[HddGauge_ConditionIndex], OBJECTIVE: (000bd4a4) and 000bd4d4[Mech_SquadOrderLineIndex]; with it set, HddGauge_PaintStatic. ES2's HddGauge_PaintIdle (DBSIM 0044ae78).

entries.name: CommBox_BeginMessage
entries.description: (display, gauge, record) in stack order, callee-cleaned: the record's id +0 into the gauge's byte +0x12d; the suffix '_' (000946b9) + ltoa of the id, a word read unsigned, after a '0' below 10, + ltoa of the record's byte +0x16, zero-extended (MOVZX at 0003e163), after '00' below 10 and '0' below 100; SpeechLine_Load(script name, voice name) with the script 'P' (000946b7) + the byte 'A' + the portrait +0x135 + suffix and the voice 'P' (000946b5) + ltoa(Pilot_VoiceBankOf(portrait)) + suffix; the slot into +0x12f; returns whether it is set. ES2's CommBox_BeginMessage (DBSIM 0044afc8).

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintPilotFrame
entries.description: (display, frame, gauge) in stack order, callee-cleaned: while the screen rect +0x8a is visible: fills the video rect +0x1d with 0x3f inside a canvas push and pop; CommBox_PushVideoClip; with +0x133 set, Bitmap_Blit of the bank's (+0x18) frame 24 + r mod 3 at its own offset pair, r the int16 Math_RandomNext (00063af4) draws on 000b5c48, sign-extended and divided unsigned (CWDE and DIV at 0003e23f-0003e247), then of the frame at its pair; with it clear, the bank's frame 6 at pair 24, then frame HddLowMemFrameMap (00094494)[frame] at the frame's pair; CommBox_PopVideoClip; the name label again inside a push and pop. ES2's HddGauge_PaintPilotFrame (DBSIM 0044b120), which blits the frame alone and publishes it for the MFD.

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintScream
entries.description: (display, gauge) in stack order, callee-cleaned: while the screen rect +0x8a is visible: at phase +0x148 0 HddGauge_PaintPilotFrame(display, 0x1b, gauge), and once the clock 000981c4 is past the deadline +0x143 the phase 1; at phase 1 HddGauge_PaintStatic, back to 0 past the deadline; on a phase change the deadline = the clock + max(5, Math_RandomBelow(000b5c48, 0x14)), compared unsigned; the clock is read once, after the visibility test, and both deadline tests are strict; +0x149 = the phase. ES2's HddGauge_PaintScream (DBSIM 0044b31c).

entries.name: HddGauge_PaintStatic
entries.description: (display, gauge) in stack order, callee-cleaned: while the screen rect +0x8a is visible: CommBox_PushVideoClip; Bitmap_Blit with flags 0 of frame +0x12e of HddStaticBank (000944d0), the dword at that index of the bank's +8 array, unchecked against the bank's count, at HddStaticFramePos (000b15fc); the frame stepped on, 5 wrapping to 0; CommBox_PopVideoClip; the name label again inside a canvas push and pop. ES2's HddGauge_PaintStatic (DBSIM 0044b3b4), which blits through VideoMode_BlitRotated and publishes the frame for the MFD.

entries.name: CommBox_OnMessageBegin
entries.description: (record) callee-cleaned: the pilot channel's begin callback. For a subject (+2) in a squadmate slot (Squad_IndexOf), CommBox_BeginMessage(HddDisplayInstance, that gauge, record); when it fails, the channel's ready +0x462 and cancelled +0x463 latches; when it succeeds, the deadline +0x143 = the clock + 0x14, state +0x13b = 1, Sound_Play(0x1c) unless Sound_IsPlaying(0x1c), and HddDisplay_ServiceCommBoxes while the display's screen rect is visible. ES2's CommBox_OnMessageBegin (DBSIM 0044b4ec).

entries.name: CommBox_OnMessageEnd
entries.description: (record) callee-cleaned: the pilot channel's end callback: for a subject (+2) in a squadmate slot (Squad_IndexOf), clears the byte +0x1c of that slot's gauge. ES2's CommBox_OnMessageEnd (DBSIM 0044b5c0).

entries.name: HddDisplay_ServiceCommBoxes
entries.description: (display) callee-cleaned: each named gauge's state +0x13b on the clock 000981c4 as read on entry, the +0x14 deadline from a second read right after it, a deadline reached at or past it. 0: while the previous state +0x13f is not 0 or CommBox_IdleRepaintPending (000946bb) is set, HddGauge_PaintIdle and Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, video rect, 1), the flag set when that copied nothing. 1: HddGauge_PaintStatic until the deadline with the latch +0x147 clear, then 2 at once. 2: on entry the channel's ready latch +0x462 and Snc_Start (0004e518), the frame -1 when that returns 0 and otherwise the speech slot's int16 +8, with the scream's (id 0x25) first deadline the clock + 5; after entry the slot's +8. At -1 the channel's cancelled latch +0x463, then for the scream the latch and state 1, otherwise state 3, deadline the clock + 0x14, Sound_Play(0x1c) unless playing and the latch when the machine's +0x93 is set; and static. Otherwise HddGauge_PaintScream or HddGauge_PaintPilotFrame. 3: static until the deadline, then 0 at once. Then +0x13f = the state. ES2's HddDisplay_ServiceCommBoxes (DBSIM 0044b5f8), which drains the .SNC queue first and drops the MFD's published block.

entries.name: CommBox_PushVideoClip
entries.description: (gauge) callee-cleaned: Cockpit_PushCanvasContext; keeps the installed render context in CommBox_SavedContext (000bd500); sets the rect +0x210-+0x21c of CommBox_ClipContext (000b15f8) to the gauge's video rect +0x1d less that context's origin +0x220/+0x224; Raster_InstallRenderContext(CommBox_ClipContext). ES2's CommBox_PushVideoClip (DBSIM 0044b83c), which also takes off the coordinate offsets.

entries.name: CommBox_PopVideoClip
entries.description: No arguments: Cockpit_PopRenderContext. Identical after normalization to ES2's CommBox_PopVideoClip (DBSIM 0044b8f8).

entries.name: HddGauge_Name
entries.description: (roster, slot) in stack order, callee-cleaned (RET 8): the dword +0x137 of gauge slot, the gauges 0x14a bytes apart from 0xf6 past the pointer at HddDisplayInstance (000944cc); the roster argument is ignored. ES2's HddGauge_Name (DBSIM 0044b900), its gauges 0x14e apart from 0x12d past 0049d230.

entries.name: HddGauge_FindByName
entries.description: (roster, name) in stack order: the index 0-2 of the first gauge, addressed as HddGauge_Name (0003e830) does, whose name +0x137 is set and is a case-insensitive prefix of name (Str_CompareNoCaseN over the gauge name's length), or -1. es2_xref finds one call, from Squad_SlotOfPilotName (0002e314). ES2's HddGauge_FindByName (DBSIM 0044b928).

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_RefreshOrders
entries.description: (screen), its arguments removed by this function: for each of the eight order rows (labels from +0x3d), the font +0 and hotkey font +0x20: ColorSchemePanels (00092d40)[0] for both when the order's availability byte (+0x131 + row) is clear or the display (HddCommandScreenInstance +4) is dark (+0x74); else [3] cpylw for the armed order (+0x5d = row + 10) and [1] cpgreen for another, each with hotkey font [2] cpred; then Label_SetTextWithHotkey(label, the order's SquadOrderAttributes byte, its SquadOrderStrings text). Clears +0x139. Draws nothing. ES2's HddCommandScreen_RefreshOrders (DBSIM 0044ddec), which also draws the armed order's plate.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_BuildMapMarkers
entries.description: (screen), its arguments removed by this function: fills the markers (+0x31) from the int16 count +0x10a on. First the route +8 of the cockpit machine's (CockpitViewInstance +0x1ff) group +0x3f, when set: for points 1 to its int16 count - 1, at most 9 (pointers from its +2), marker i takes frame i at +0x24, the point at +0x3c-+0x44 and HddMarker_SetSize (00041fac)(marker, 9). Then each object of LiveObjectList by class +0x162 and side (group +0x3f's +0x14): class 0 the player's own 0x12, a squad slot n (Squad_IndexOf) 0x1b + 9n, another on side 0 0x36, another side 9, size 7; class 2 0x3f, size 5; class 1 with type index (+0x188's int16 +0) 5, 6 or 8: 0x4b on side 0, 0x49 else, size 7, +0x4d 7; class 1 otherwise 0x4a or 0x48, size 13, +0x4d 13; other classes none. A marker stores the frame +0x24, the object +0x38, the class +0x48, its size, the ranged byte +0x4c (class 1); a ranged one also +0x4f 0, the color +0x51 (0x32 on side 0, 0x35 else) and +0x57 25000. Sets +0x109 and frees the markers from the count to 74 with Mem_Delete, leaving the pointers. It does not compare the count with 75. ES2's HddCommandScreen_BuildMapMarkers (DBSIM 0044ded8) with HddCommandScreen_AddObjectMarker (DBSIM 0044e080) inlined, without ES2's nav marker or class 3.

entries.name: HddCommandScreen_DrawMap
entries.description: (screen), its arguments removed by this function: keeps the installed render context (000bdbda), installs the map's (HddCommandScreen_InstallMapContext) and fills its rect with the brush {0, 0x36}. Unless the display is dark (+0x74): center +0x18/+0x1c = the cockpit machine's +0x20/+0x24 plus the pan offsets +0x114/+0x118, unclamped, setting +0x30 and +0x125-+0x12d when center or scale +0x20 changed; the camera +0x14's position = center and scale, Raster_InstallViewProjection, Raster_SetModelTransform(0). With +0x30: the origin's screen point to +0x24/+0x28 and the x span to (800000, 800000) to +0x2c, +0x30 cleared. Grid lines in the pen {0, 0x37}, 50000-unit squares: at the origin + ((i * span) >> 4) for i = 0, 1, ... across the viewport, then at the origin - (span >> 4) and + ((i * span) >> 4) for i = -2, -3, ... the other way, on x and on y. The grown box +0x160-+0x16c framed with the brush {4, 0x35}. Palette_SetRampsToRange({0x38, 1}, 1, 14), then each Zone_ShapeObjects object drawn by its slot +4, the walk ending at Zone_ShapeCount or a null entry, with the word its shape instance's (+0x2e) +8 points at set to 1 for the draw and 0 after. Then each marker: a route marker at +0x3c; an object skipped on a side other than 0 when +0x9e or +0x93 is set, else at its +0x20 when +0x8f is set or it is on side 0 with its group's +0x16 clear, else at (+0x164, +0x168, 0) when bit 0x20 of 000981c4 and +0xa1 are clear, else skipped; placed by Widget_MoveTo (000438a4) at the projected point less its half-size through HddMap_ToViewport, the old top-left kept at +0x2e/+0x32; for the selected squadmate's machine (g_SquadmateMachines[+0x105]) a line from the marker's center to the current pick (+0xa6, HudColorTable_Get(slot)) or the saved pick (+0xa5, that less 1), then not painted while +0x17d and HddCommandScreen_BlinkPhase (00094867) are set; for a ranged marker +0x53 = Math_FastMagnitude3D(point less center, z less scale); then its slot +4. The chosen unit +0x15c's marker, when placed, framed with the brush {4, 0x3c} grown by its +0x4a. Reinstalls the kept context. ES2's HddCommandScreen_DrawMap (DBSIM 0044e30c), which clamps, blits a terrain raster, has 200,000-unit squares, frames the ungrown box and paints the nav marker.

It reads the flag bytes through the object + 0x8c (+0x93 at +7, +0x92 at +6). ES2's HddCommandScreen_IsEligibleUnit (DBSIM 0044f014), which calls HddCommandScreen_IsOnMap (DBSIM 0044f09c) where this calls HddCommandScreen_IsOnMap (00041bb8).

entries.name: HddMarker_Paint
entries.description: (marker), its arguments removed by this function: slot +4 of HddMarkerVtable (0009495e). Inside the canvas push and pop, installs the screen's (+0x20) map context and takes the rect's top-left back with HddMap_FromViewport. Frame, from the array at HddMarker_Icons (00094870) +8: a route marker's +0x24; for class 0 or 2, the heading +0xa's octant (0 within 0x1000 of 0, else 7 down in 0x2000 steps), x and y both plus the signed byte HddMarker_OctantNudge (00094874)[octant], frame +0x24 + octant + 1, or +0x24 when destroyed (+0x93); class 1 +0x24; any other class draws nothing. Not ranged (+0x4c): Bitmap_Blit(frame, 0, point), +0x4a = +0x2a. Ranged: a = (+0x57 << 7) / +0x53; below +0x4f, Gfx_PlotPixel in +0x51 and +0x4a = 0; below the frame's int16 +4, Bitmap_BlitScaled(frame, (a, a), 0, the point plus the half-size less a >> 1) and +0x4a = a >> 1; else blitted whole. ES2's HddMarker_Paint (DBSIM 0044f194), which draws a box where this scales the icon, rings scanners, and nudges and maps octants through tables.

entries.description: (screen, display, damage column, screen rect): allocates 0xec bytes with Mem_New (000015a4) when given none, returning 0 when that fails; HDDisplay_Ctor (0003c228)(screen, display, screen rect); HDDDamageVtable (00094aaa) at +0xc. Then HddDamageScreen_SetView (000423d8)(screen, 0); +0x78 = -1; +0xe0 and +0xe4 = the display's subject +0x4e1; the int16 +0x8e, +0xb4 and +0xcc = 1; and the no-subject label +0xe8 in cpred over 40 pixels either side of the screen rect's middle x and from its middle y to that + 10, flags 2, filled 0x3b. entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Update
entries.description: (screen, copy): draws the damage page. With the display dark (its +0x74) it fills the screen rect 0x1f and returns. Otherwise the subject +0xe4 = the display's +0x4e1, and a new subject (HddDamageScreen_SetView (000423d8) again), view or row offset makes a full redraw; with no subject it redraws only on a new subject or view. By the view it picks the names, the readouts from Mech_ReadDamageReadouts (0001583c) (entries 1-19, 20-31 or from 32) and the .PDG view (0, 1 or 0); for view 2 it first copies each non-null mount's WeaponMount_GetDisplayName (0000aa9c) into the next 8-byte slot of HddDamage_WeaponNameBuffer (000b1634) and points HddDamage_WeaponNames (000b160c) at it by mount index. Not a full redraw and the readouts unchanged: it returns. A full redraw fills the screen rect 0x1f, runs HddDamageScreen_SetSubjectCaption (0003e9b8), sets the no-subject label's text with no subject, else blits the doll and HddDamageScreen_BlitWeaponIcons (000432b0) and recolors with PaperDoll_RecolorRect (00030818) (views 0 and 1: icon rects 0x38 to 0x32; view 2: the view 0x36-0x38 and other region colors to 0x32, icons 0x36 to 0x38). Then each row, at most 12 from the offset: tints its region with PaperDoll_RecolorRectFromArt (00030ab4) or its icon with PaperDoll_RecolorRect in mode 0 by Damage_PickRegionTint (00030dc4), view 0's regions 0 and 2 on the mean with the next index and 1 and 3 not at all, and sets the name and value labels (ltoa (00064720) of the percent) in the state's ColorSchemePanels font; saves the readouts at +0x8c. Each redrawn rect goes to the other page through Widget_DrawToCockpit (0002b058) when copy is set. ES2's HddDamageScreen_Update (DBSIM 00450c54), which shows 13 rows, picks flyer names and pairs region 0 and 1 alone.

entries.name: HddDamageScreen_Show

entries.name: CockpitClock_Ctor
entries.description: (clock, cockpit, rect): allocates the 0x8a-byte cockpit clock when given none (returning 0 when that fails); builds it with PanelGauge_Ctor (00031318)(clock, cockpit, rect + 0x10) and stores the vtable 00094b5a at +0x76. Opens the HERC's .TTM with Ttm_Open(CockpitTtmManager (00092d70), 0, 0, Path_WithExtension(ttm (00094b72), eight characters of CockpitOverride_Name (000925f8)'s string when CockpitOverride_Name (000925f8) is set, else of +0x58 of the type record +0x188 of CockpitViewInstance's +0x1ff)), takes the handle as a signed byte, and when that handle's entry of the table +5 holds a script stores CockpitViewInstance's +4 at the script's +0x1bd; a failed open's 0xff reads the dword before the table. Copies cpwincrk (00094b76) into the name buffer; sets the strings 00, 00 and : at 000bd504, 000bd508 and 000bd50c; makes three labels with Label_Ctor(0, ColorSchemePanels (00092d40)) at +0x7a, +0x7e and +0x82, each passed to Label_SetRect with 1, 4 and 2 respectively, rect + 0x10 and the point (1, 0), (1, 0) and (0, 0), and their +0x1c set to 0x3f, 0 and 0; sets +0x86 to 000981c4 + 30. es2_xref finds one call, from CockpitClock_Create (0002ce98).

entries.name: CockpitClock_Tick
entries.description: (clock): slot +0xc of the clock's vtable 00094b5a, entered at 000435bf. Sets the mark +0x75 to 2 while the published view manager's +0x18 is set; while +0x75 is set draws the rect from +4 of the hour label +0x7a to +0xc of the minute label +0x7e with Widget_DrawToCockpit(0, rect, 0) and clears it; when the count 000981c4 is above +0x86, compared unsigned, calls CockpitClock_Advance (00043658), sets +0x86 to the count as read before the call + 30 and +0x75 to 1.

entries.name: CockpitClock_Advance
entries.description: (clock): toggles the byte 00094b56 and, when it becomes 1, adds a minute to the digits HH (000bd504-000bd505) and MM (000bd508-000bd509): minutes 00 to 59, hours 00 to 24, the minute after 24:59 setting all four to 0. When CockpitView_RectCornerVisible(hour label +0x7a's +4) is nonzero, between Cockpit_PushCanvasContext and Cockpit_PopRenderContext sets the hour label's text to 000bd504 and the minute label's (+0x7e) to 000bd508 with Label_SetText, and the colon label's (+0x82) to 000bd50c while 00094b56 is 1. es2_xref finds calls from CockpitClock_Update (000435b0) and CockpitClock_Tick (000435c0), through the padding entry 00043657.

While the byte 000bd512 is set, with t the dword 000981c4: when the record's word +8 equals the dword CockpitMouse_LastButtons (000bd538), calls Cursor_SyncPosition (000669dc)(record) while Cursor_FollowsMouse (00094c5b) is set and, when t is above the dword CockpitMouse_LastEventTime (00094cc8), CockpitMouseQueue_Push (00044830)(t, record) by its padding 0004482d; otherwise stores the word in CockpitMouse_LastButtons (000bd538) and calls CockpitMouseQueue_Push (00044830)(the clock 000981c4, record); either way stores t in CockpitMouse_LastEventTime (00094cc8). ES2's CockpitMouse_OnEvent (DBSIM 00452cb4), which reads Time_GetCoarseTicks and stores the time outside the test of its live byte.

entries.name: CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue
entries.description: No arguments: swaps the queue pointers CockpitMouseQueue_Back (000bd530) and CockpitMouseQueue_Front (000bd534), zeroes the count of the one CockpitMouseQueue_Back (000bd530) now holds and, for each 14-byte record {x, y, buttons, time} of the one CockpitMouseQueue_Front (000bd534) holds, with r the root Widget_ActiveRoot (00094c54): Widget_ClickButtons (00094b84) = the buttons; when the point differs from CockpitMouse_LastPoint (000b16c0)/000b16c4, stores it there, calls Cursor_SyncPosition (000669dc) while TapePlayback (000b5b76) and Cursor_FollowsMouse (00094c5b) are set, stores the point less r's +0x227/+0x22b in CockpitMouse_CanvasPoint (000b16d4)/000b16d8 and, with Widget_DragCapture (00094c5a) clear, calls Widget_TrackPressedWidget (00043f68)(r, point) when Widget_HitTest (000437d0)(r, point) passes, or with it set calls slot +0x1c of the captured entry (index Widget_PressedIndex (00094c58) of r's list +0x252) with the point less r's +0/+4 and Widget_Repaint (0004410c); clears CockpitMouse_DoubleClick (00094c5c); a left press (bit 0 set, the byte CockpitMouse_LeftHeld (000bd50e) clear) sets CockpitMouse_LeftHeld (000bd50e) and calls Widget_OnMouseDown (00043e00)(r, point); a right press sets CockpitMouse_RightHeld (000bd510); a left release clears CockpitMouse_LeftHeld (000bd50e), sets CockpitMouse_DoubleClick (00094c5c) when time - the dword CockpitMouse_LastLeftRelease (00094c60) is below CockpitMouse_DoubleClickTicks (000bd518), stores time in CockpitMouse_LastLeftRelease (00094c60) and the buttons | 1 in Widget_ClickButtons (00094b84); a right release the same with CockpitMouse_RightHeld (000bd510), CockpitMouse_LastRightRelease (00094c64) and | 2; after a release calls Widget_OnMouseUp (00043eac)(r, point) with Widget_DragCapture (00094c5a) clear, or else sets the captured entry's +0x17 to 0, repaints it, clears Widget_DragCapture (00094c5a), calls its slot +0xc with what its slot +0x14 returns and sets Widget_PressedIndex (00094c58) to -1. Returns the queue CockpitMouseQueue_Front (000bd534) holds. ES2's CockpitMouse_ProcessQueue (DBSIM 00452d18), which clears its button word after each record. es2_xref finds one call, from Input_ReadPlayerInput (0004cb14).

entries.name: CockpitMouseQueue_Push
entries.description: (time, record) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function, entered also at its padding 0004482d: returns 0 when the count of the queue CockpitMouseQueue_Back (000bd530) points at is 99; otherwise appends a 14-byte entry to its buffer, the record's x and y dwords, its buttons word and the time dword at +0xa, raises the count and returns 1. ES2's CockpitMouseQueue_Push (DBSIM 00453034). es2_xref finds calls from CockpitMouse_OnEvent (00044464) and Input_ReadPlayerInput (0004cb14), whose playback passes each recorded record with its recorded time.

entries.name: CockpitMouse_StaticInitNoOp
entries.description: Frameless, with no Ghidra function: RET. The static constructor table's entry 000adc50, the cockpit mouse file's last code, followed by three zero bytes.

entries.name: WidgetStyles_Load
entries.description: (path), callee-cleaned: opens path (VolRStream_CtorFromPath), reads the int16 count to 000bd53c and, when it is not 0, __vec_new builds that many 64-byte records with WidgetStyle_ElementCtor (00044910) at 00094ccc and reads them one at a time; destroys the stream. Checks neither the stream status nor the length, and frees no earlier table.

entries.name: WidgetStyle_ElementCtor
entries.description: (this) callee-cleaned: the __vec_new element constructor WidgetStyles_Load (00044880) passes (by way of the padding entry 0004490f) for the 64-byte STYLES.DAT records. Allocates 0x40 bytes when this is null; writes nothing and returns this.

entries.name: WidgetStyles_StaticDtor
entries.description: No arguments, a static exit routine: when the style table 00094ccc is not 0, __vec_delete(0, 0x40, 7, the table) and 0 to 00094ccc.

entries.name: CornerFrame_Draw
entries.description: (style, rect by value) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: draws a bevelled frame from a 64-byte STYLES.DAT record. Fills (x0+3, y0+3)-(x1-3, y1-3), ordered, with Raster_FillRect under the brush {0, style dword +0} at +0x22c of the render context the display's (000bdd28) +0x44 less 4 points at, then puts the brush back; then CornerFrame_DrawEdgeRing (00044adc) with (first, grow, inset) (1, 0, 0), (5, -2, 1) and (9, -4, 2), and CornerFrame_DrawCorners (00044c64), each given the rect by value through Rect_CopyCtor (00044aac). ES2's CornerFrame_Draw (DBSIM 00453240). es2_xref finds one call, from PanelButton_Paint (000468e0).

entries.name: Rect_CopyCtor
entries.description: (copy, rect) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function, also entered at its padding 00044aab: copies the four int32 of the rect into the copy, allocating 0x10 bytes with Mem_New when the copy is null and returning 0 when that fails; returns the copy. CornerFrame_Draw (00044954) passes its rect by value through it.

entries.name: CornerFrame_DrawEdgeRing
entries.description: (style, first, grow, inset, rect by value) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function, also entered at its padding 00044ada: one ring of four one-pixel edges with Raster_DrawLine, each under the pen {0, colour} at the render context's +0x228 (restored after) and skipped when that colour dword is 0. With left = x0 + inset, top = y0 + inset, w = x1 - x0 + grow and h = y1 - y0 + grow: dword style[first] the left edge (left, top+1)-(left, top+h-1), style[first+1] the top edge (left+1, top)-(left+w-1, top), style[first+2] the right edge (left+w, top+1)-(left+w, top+h-1), style[first+3] the bottom edge (left+1, top+h)-(left+w-1, top+h). ES2's CornerFrame_DrawEdgeRing (DBSIM 004533a4). es2_xref finds three calls, from CornerFrame_Draw (00044954).

entries.name: CornerFrame_DrawCorners
entries.description: (style, rect by value) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: Bitmap_Blit with flags 0 of four frames of the dba\corners bank WidgetCorners (000bd53e): frame int16 +0x34 at (x0, y0), +0x36 at (x1 - w, y0), +0x38 at (x0, y1 - h), +0x3a at (x1 - w, y1 - h), w and h being the style's int16 +0x3c and +0x3e. ES2's CornerFrame_DrawCorners (DBSIM 00453518). es2_xref finds one call, from CornerFrame_Draw (00044954).

entries.name: CockpitFont_Load
entries.description: (path, slot) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: opens the path as a VolRStream (VolRStream_CtorFromPath), stores ClassItem_LoadResource's result in *slot and destroys the stream. entries.name: Raster_FrameRectColour

ES2's Raster_FillFrameRectColours (DBSIM 00453738). No caller, stored pointer or vtable slot found by es2_xref.

entries.description: (colour, end, start) in stack order, each point two int32 by value, its arguments removed by this function, the colour an int16: Raster_DrawLine(start, end) under the pen {0, colour} at the render context's (000bdbda) +0x228, then puts the pen back. ES2's Raster_DrawLineColour (DBSIM 00453798). es2_xref finds four calls, from AlertPanel_SetTitleText (000461ec).

entries.name: StringTable_Ctor
entries.description: (table), callee-cleaned: allocates 0x10 bytes when given none (returning 0 when that fails), clears the buffer +0, cursor +4, length +8 and the int16 counters +0xc and +0xe, and returns the table. ES2's StringTable_Ctor (DBSIM 004537e0), which allocates nothing.

entries.name: OwnedArray_Dtor
entries.description: (holder, flags) in stack order, callee-cleaned: with the holder non-null, Mem_Delete (000015f8) of the block at +0 when that is non-null, then of the holder when bit 0 of flags is set. ES2's OwnedArray_Dtor (DBSIM 00453804), which also counts destructors.

entries.name: StringTable_LoadFromFile
entries.description: (table, path) in stack order, callee-cleaned: opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, runs StringTable_Load(table, stream), destroys the stream and returns StringTable_Load's result.

entries.name: StringTable_Load
entries.description: (table, stream) in stack order, callee-cleaned: reads the table's byte size (4 bytes) into +8 through the stream's vtable +0x1c, allocates that many bytes at +0, reads them, sets the cursor +4 to the buffer and returns 1. StringTable_ReadNext and StringTable_LoadGroup read the table it fills.

entries.name: StringTable_ReadNext
entries.description: (table, &attributes, &text) in stack order, callee-cleaned: reads the next string of a loaded .STR table {buffer +0, cursor +4, length +8, group count +0xc, index +0xe}. Returns 0 at the end of the buffer. At a group's start (+0xc is 0) it reads the group's int16 count from the cursor and zeroes the index. While the index is below the count it stores the address past the string's int16 length in *text, steps over the string to its attribute-count byte, and when attributes is non-null stores the address after that byte in *attributes and steps over the attributes; with a null attributes it leaves the cursor on the first attribute byte. It then counts the string and returns 1. At the group's end it zeroes the count and the index and returns 0. ES2's StringTable_ReadNext (DBSIM 004538d4), statement for statement.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 00045004, against ES2's StringTable_ReadNext

entries.name: StringTable_LoadGroup
entries.description: (table, attributeDestination, capacity, destination) in stack order, callee-cleaned: reads the int16 group count at the cursor and calls StringTable_ReadNext that many times, filling consecutive destination entries and, when attributeDestination is non-null, consecutive attribute entries; then zeroes the group count +0xc and returns the count it read. capacity is not read. ES2's StringTable_LoadGroup (DBSIM 0045395c).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM disassembly at 000450b0, against ES2's StringTable_LoadGroup

entries.name: StrTable_FirstString
entries.description: (table), callee-cleaned: the loaded buffer (*table) + 4, the first entry's text, or 0 when nothing is loaded. Identical after normalization to ES2's StrTable_FirstString (DBSIM 004539b0).

entries.name: StrTable_NextString
entries.description: (table, string) in stack order, callee-cleaned: while string lies inside the buffer (*table + length table[2]), the string after it: string + its int16 length prefix (string - 2) is the attribute count byte, and the next text starts that count + 3 bytes on; else 0. Identical after normalization to ES2's StrTable_NextString (DBSIM 004539cc).

entries.name: StrTable_GetAttributes
entries.description: (table, string) in stack order, callee-cleaned: the entry's attribute bytes, the byte after the count byte at string + its int16 length prefix, or 0 when the count is 0 or string lies past the buffer. ES2's StrTable_GetAttributes (DBSIM 00453a08), its tests in the other order.

entries.name: AlertPanel_CtorBase
entries.description: (panel, rect, keepsScreen) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: the in-mission panels' base constructor. Allocates 0x10 bytes when the panel is null; builds the rect region at +0x10 (vtables 00094d8a to 00094dfe, type 0), StringTable_Ctor (00044f14) at +0x30, GLViewport_Ctor at +0x44, the title bar rect at +0x2ba and GLCursor_Ctor at +0x2ca; stores AlertVtable (00094e26) at +0x314; clears the widget count +0x2b5 and the close byte +0x2b9; copies the rect to +0 and to the render context's rect +0x254, sets its clip mode +0x24c and translation flag +0x250 to 1, +0x264 and +0x268 to 0 and its brush +0x270 to Alert_FillBrush (000b1718); the region's rect is (0, 0, x1 - x0, y1 - y0); with keepsScreen set, a buffer of Rect_PixelCount(region) bytes at +0x28, asserting 'Alert: can't allocate buffer.' (alert.cpp line 0x3b) when Mem_New fails, else 0; +0x2c = 0; Widget_ActiveRoot kept at +0x285; CTLWindow_Ctor (00043cac)(0, panel) at +0x281; the display's draw page (+0x3c of 000bdd28) at +0x289; -1 at +0x2e3 (the cancel widget) and 1 at +0x313. ES2's AlertPanel_CtorBase (DBSIM 00454174), whose vptr is at +0 and its rect at +4. es2_xref finds calls from StatusAlertPanel_Ctor (00046efc), PreferencesPanel_Ctor (00047578), ControlsPanel_Ctor (00048408), 00049154 and ObjectivesPanel_Ctor (0004a1b4).

entries.name: Alert_Dtor
entries.description: (panel, flags) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: the in-mission panels' base destructor. Stores AlertVtable (00094e26) at +0x314; frees each of the +0x2b5 widgets at +0x28d and the screen buffer +0x28 when set; destroys +0x2c when set through its slot +0x1c with 3; frees the title label +0x40; clears +0x2ce; GLCursor_Dtor(+0x2ca, 2); stores the vtables 00094e7e and 00094dae at the render context +0x44; OwnedArray_Dtor (00044f48)(+0x30, 2); stores 00094dfe, 00094dd6 and 00094dae at the region +0x10. It tests neither the panel nor the flags and frees nothing of the panel itself. ES2's Alert_Dtor (DBSIM 00454394). es2_xref finds calls from CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand, Sim_DispatchCommand and Sim_MainTick, each with 3 after a panel's run, and from GeneralAlert_Dtor (000472b0), PreferencesPanel_Dtor (00047a14), ControlsPanel_Dtor (000487b4), 00049678 and ObjectivesPanel_Dtor (0004a480) with 0.

Slot +0x1c of the vtable 00094e7e, the GLViewport table Alert_Dtor (00045d0c) stores at the panel's render context; alert.cpp's copy of GLViewport's destructor.

Caller found by es2_xref: Sim_StartMission (0005a9dc), at 0005abc2.

entries.name: AlertPanel_Enter
entries.description: (panel) in stack order, its argument removed by this function: puts a panel up. Copies the 0x2b bytes of PlayerInputBlock to +0x2e8; Input_LatchButton (0004d8c8)(1, 1) to (1, 4); AlertPanel_SetFocus (00046470)(panel, -1); Widget_ClearPressed (00044310)(the panel's root +0x281); keeps the render context 000bdbda at +0x27d and installs the panel's +0x44; sets the display's source and draw pages to its +0x88; keeps Cursor_FollowsMouse at +0x2de and sets it; calls AlertPanel_EnterHook (00094d80) when set; the first time, loads dci\alert into AlertPanel_CursorImage (00094d7c) with Cursor_LoadWrapper; hides the cursor (slot 31); with a buffer at +0x28, Region_Save of the region +0x14 into it, its rect moved by minus the panel's corner for the call, since Region_SaveRect (00066470) and Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch (0006aa70) each add the panel's render context's translation, the corner; the panel's slot +4; AlertPanel_LoadCursor (000463c0)(panel, the alert cursor); shows the cursor (slot 30); adds 1 to AlertPanel_OpenCount (00094d78). ES2's AlertPanel_Enter (DBSIM 00454630) without the message ports and the present timer. es2_xref finds calls from StatusAlertPanel_RunModal (0004730c), PreferencesPanel_Run (00047a88), ControlsPanel_Run (00048810), 000496f0 and ObjectivesPanel_RunModal (0004a4ec).

entries.description: (panel) in stack order, its argument removed by this function: takes a panel down. Clears Cursor_FollowsMouse and hides the cursor; with a buffer at +0x28, Region_Restore of the region +0x14 at +0x18; AlertPanel_RestoreCursorImage (00046428); Cursor_FollowsMouse back from +0x2de, showing the cursor when it is set; calls AlertPanel_LeaveHook (00094d84) when set; installs the render context +0x27d and makes +0x289 the display's draw page; WidgetRoot_Delete (00044350)(+0x281) and, when +0x285 is set, Widget_ClearPressed(+0x285); copies the 0x2b bytes at +0x2e8 back to PlayerInputBlock; with a mouse device, Mouse_SetPosition to the saved pointer +0x2ea, +0x2ee and Cursor_SyncPosition; takes 1 from AlertPanel_OpenCount (00094d78). ES2's AlertPanel_Leave (DBSIM 004548ac) without the present, the two flags and the message ports. es2_xref finds calls from StatusAlertPanel_RunModal (0004730c), PreferencesPanel_Run (00047a88), ControlsPanel_Run (00048810), 000496f0 and ObjectivesPanel_RunModal (0004a4ec).

entries.description: (panel, text) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function, slot +8 of AlertVtable (00094e26): frames the title bar rect +0x2ba with Raster_DrawLineColour (00044ec0), the top (x0, y0)-(x1, y0) and left (x0, y0)-(x0, y1) edges in colour 0x10, the right (x1, y1)-(x1, y0) in 0x1b and the bottom (x1, y1)-(x0, y1) in 0x1c; Bitmap_Blit with flags 0 of WidgetCorners (000bd53e) frames 0 to 3 at (x0, y0), (x1 - 4, y0), (x0, y1 - 4) and (x1 - 4, y1 - 4); then Label_SetText (0003114c) on the title label +0x40. ES2's slot, AlertPanel_SetTitleText (DBSIM 00454b58), sets the text alone.

ES2's AlertPanel_LoadCursor (DBSIM 00454b70) without the scroll-window path.

entries.description: (panel) in stack order, its argument removed by this function: while +0x313 is set, Cursor_SetImage (00066948)(the kept bitmap +0x2ce plus 4, or 0 when it is 0; +0x2d2). ES2's AlertPanel_RestoreCursorImage (DBSIM 00454c10) without the scroll-window path. es2_xref finds one call, from AlertPanel_Leave (000460b8).

entries.name: AlertPanel_SetFocus
entries.description: (panel, index) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function, also entered at its padding 0004646e: for index -1, with a mouse device (Input_GetMouseDevice_Thunk), runs Input_ReadPlayerInput (0004cb14) and takes the first of the +0x2b5 widgets at +0x28d whose rect holds the block's pointer (+2, +6), edges included, else -1: the pointer in screen pixels against the widgets' panel-local rects, without the panel's corner; for another index, puts the pointer on the widget's centre plus the panel's origin (x0 + ((x1 - x0) >> 1) + panel x0, likewise y) with Mouse_SetPosition when there is a mouse device and Cursor_SyncPosition either way. Stores the index at +0x2df. ES2's AlertPanel_SetFocus (DBSIM 00454c7c).

entries.description: (panel, widget) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: finds the widget in the +0x28d list (count +0x2b5) and focuses its index with AlertPanel_SetFocus (00046470); does nothing for a widget not in the list. ES2's AlertPanel_FocusChild (DBSIM 00454d48). es2_xref finds one call, from PanelButton_OnClick (000469ac).

entries.name: AlertPanel_PressWidget
entries.description: (panel, flags, index) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: unless the widget at that index of +0x28d is in state 2 or 3 (int16 +0x17), calls its click slot +0xc (vtable at +0x1c) with the flags. It makes no other call: ES2's AlertPanel_PressWidget (DBSIM 00454dcc), which refuses state 2 alone, also flashes the widget on the panel's root.

entries.name: AlertPanel_HandleEvent
entries.description: (panel, block) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function, slot +0x14 of AlertVtable (00094e26), also entered at its padding 0004666e: button 0 (+0x15) presses the focused widget +0x2df with AlertPanel_PressWidget (0004662c)(flags 1), or focuses widget 0 with AlertPanel_SetFocus (00046470) when the focus is -1, then Input_LatchButton (0004d8c8)(1, 1); else button 1 (+0x16) runs AlertPanel_FocusNext (000465d8) and Input_LatchButton(1, 2); else the command word, by REPNE SCASD in the 5 dwords at 00094eec: 0x01 presses the cancel widget +0x2e3 unless it is -1, 0x0f focuses the next, 0x20f the previous AlertPanel_FocusPrevious (00046600), 0x1c does what button 0 does without the latch, and 0x52 focuses the next while the preferences byte 000bd56c is set. Returns 1 for either button and for each of the five codes, also when the case acts on nothing (0x01 with the cancel widget -1, 0x52 with the byte clear), and 0 for any other code. ES2's AlertPanel_HandleEvent (DBSIM 00454e10), whose previous-widget code is 0x80f.

entries.description: (height, width, y, x) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: writes (x, y, x + width, y + height) to AlertPanel_RectScratch (000b1724), setting its first-use byte 000b1720, and returns its address. ES2's AlertPanel_SetRect (DBSIM 00454ef8).

entries.description: (height, width) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: AlertPanel_SetRect (0004675c) at x = (000b1710 - width) >> 1 and y = (000b1714 - height) >> 1, the x1 and y1 of AlertPanel_ScreenRect (000b1708), 319 and 199. ES2's AlertPanel_CenterRect (DBSIM 00454f34).

No reference found by es2_xref. ES2's PreferencesPanel_Revert (DBSIM 004574e0) with seven options for ES2's nine.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_Ctor
entries.description: (panel, rect, keepsScreen) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: the controls panel the preferences panel's CONTROLS raises. Allocates 0x3a6 bytes with Mem_New when panel is null (returning 0 when that fails); a 222 x 109 rect, centered by AlertPanel_CenterRect (0004679c) or at the rect's point by AlertPanel_SetRect (0004675c); AlertPanel_CtorBase (00045988)(panel, that rect, keepsScreen); ControlsAlertVtable (000952c6) at +0x314; the plate, frame 0 of dba\ctl_alrt (ClassItem_LoadFromFile (0005760c)), at +0x2c; str\ctl_alrt into the string table +0x30 (StringTable_LoadFromFile (00044f78)) and six groups with StringTable_LoadGroup (000450b0): the title to +0x318, seven captions to +0x31c, NO and YES to +0x338, OFF and ON to +0x340, ten stick models to +0x348, five stick controls to +0x370. Seven buttons, PanelButton_Ctor (000467c8)(0, index, panel, rect) on the int16 tables 00095244 (x), 00095254 (y), 00095264 (w) and 00095274 (h), each with a caption label in WidgetFont_Cpylw centered by Label_SetRect (00031080) with flags 2 and margin (0, -2), the word of the table 00095284, registered with Widget_RegisterClickable (000443d4) on the root +0x281 and added to the widget list +0x28d in order. The title label at +0x40 as the preferences panel's. Five readout labels at +0x384 in WidgetFont_Green6x8 on the tables 00095294 to 000952b8, flags 1, margin (2, -2), background 0x3f. Clears the action +0x398 and makes the last widget, DONE, the cancel widget +0x2e3. Returns the panel. es2_xref finds one call, from PreferencesPanel_Run (00047a88), passing (a stack object, 0, 1). ES2's ControlsPanel_Ctor (DBSIM 00457d1c) builds a panel of the same name with other rows.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_Dtor
entries.description: (panel, flags) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: returns for a null panel; stores ControlsAlertVtable (000952c6), frees the five readout labels +0x384 with Mem_Delete, runs Alert_Dtor (00045d0c)(panel, 0) and frees the panel when bit 0 of flags is set. es2_xref finds one call, from PreferencesPanel_Run (00047a88), which passes 2.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_Run
entries.description: (panel), slot +0xc of ControlsAlertVtable (000952c6): the controls panel's loop. Copies options 7, 8, 10, 9 and 11 to +0x39c to +0x3a0; +0x3a1 = 2 when option 7 is 2, else 0; +0x3a2 = option 8, or 1 for 0; +0x3a3 = option 9; +0x3a4 and +0x3a5 = options 7 and 9 as applied. AlertPanel_Enter (00045f00), AlertPanel_SetFocus (00046470)(panel, 0); until the close byte +0x2b9 is set: Input_ReadPlayerInput (0004cb14), the block to slot +0x14; for the action +0x398 (the button index plus 1): 1 steps option 7 modulo 6, Prefs_StepOption (0004a988) or with the right-button byte +0x2e7 Prefs_StepOptionBack (0004a9d0), once more forward when that gives 0 with the block's button 0 (+0x15) held; for 0, with the panel's option 8 +0x39d not 0, it keeps that at +0x3a2 and sets option 8 to 0 (Prefs_SetOption (0004a914)), leaving the RCS byte +0x39f alone; for any other model it puts option 8 back from +0x3a2 when it is 0, and then at 2 keeps the RCS byte +0x39f, when set, at +0x3a3 and XORs it with 1, and at any other model sets it from +0x3a3 when that is set; 2, with option 7 not 0, steps option 8 modulo 3 forward or back until it is not 0; 3 toggles option 10 (Prefs_ToggleOption (0004a94c)); 4 toggles option 9 and, turned on with option 7 at 2, sets option 7 to 1 with +0x3a1 = 2, or turned off with +0x3a1 at 2, sets option 7 back to 2 and +0x3a1 = 0; 5 toggles option 11; 6, CALIBRATE, with option 9 set or option 7 not 0, ControlsPanel_ApplyDevices (00048e98), the calibration panel on the stack (00049154(that, panel, 1)), its loop 000496f0, the focus to the cancel widget, and its destructor 00049678(that, 2); 7, DONE, ControlsPanel_ApplyDevices and Prefs_CommitOptions (0004a83c)(1). Each changed row is redrawn with ControlsPanel_RefreshRow (00048ce4). Then each widget's per-frame slot +0x10. AlertPanel_Leave (000460b8); returns bit 0 of the close byte. ES2's ControlsPanel_Run (DBSIM 00458650) binds stick buttons.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_Paint
entries.description: (panel), slot +4 of ControlsAlertVtable (000952c6): Bitmap_Blit (00067048)(the plate +0x2c, 0, the region's rect +0x18); the title through slot +8 with +0x318; each widget's paint, slot +4 of its +0x1c table; then ControlsPanel_RefreshRow (00048ce4) for rows 1 to 5. ES2's ControlsPanel_Paint (DBSIM 00458c68), on twelve rows.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_RefreshRow
entries.description: (panel, row) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: sets one of the controls panel's five readout labels from the panel's copies of the option bytes, between g_RasterRoutines slots 31 and 30 (0009df50, 0009df4c): row 1 Label_SetText(+0x384, the stick model +0x348[byte +0x39c]), row 2 (+0x388, the stick's control +0x370[+0x39d]), row 3 (+0x38c, NO or YES +0x338[+0x39e]), row 4 (+0x390, +0x338[+0x39f]), row 5 (+0x394, OFF or ON +0x340[+0x3a0]). ES2's ControlsPanel_RefreshRow (DBSIM 00458d20) has twelve rows.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_OnClick
entries.description: (panel, flags, child), slot +0x10 of ControlsAlertVtable (000952c6), which a button's click calls: stores bit 1 of flags, the right button, at +0x2e7; for the child at index 0 to 6 of the widget list +0x28d stores index + 1 at the action +0x398, and for 6, DONE, also sets the close byte +0x2b9 to 3. ES2's ControlsPanel_OnClick (DBSIM 00458ebc) selects button rows.

entries.name: ControlsPanel_GetButtonCaption
entries.description: (panel, index), slot +0x18 of ControlsAlertVtable (000952c6): returns the caption +0x31c[index].

entries.name: ControlsPanel_ApplyDevices
entries.description: (panel): when the panel's option 7 (+0x39c) or option 9 (+0x39f) differs from the copy last applied (+0x3a4, +0x3a5), destroys the recorded joystick devices (Input_GetJoystickDevice_Thunk (0004c63c), Input_GetJoystick2Device_Thunk (0004c644), JoystickDevice_Dtor (0004b7a8) with 3) and builds them for option 7 (000bd569) as Input_CreateJoystickDevices (0004af0c) does, each constructor with mode 1: 1 IMJoystick1_Ctor (0004be30), 2 that and IMJoystick2_Ctor (0004be94), 3 IMThrustmasterFCS_Ctor (0004bef8), 4 IMFlightstick_Ctor (0004c054), 5 IMFlightstickPro_Ctor (0004c114); with option 9 (000bd56b) set, IMThrustmasterRCS_Ctor (0004bfe0) as the second, or for option 7 at 2 option 9 cleared (Prefs_SetOption (0004a914)(1, 0, 9)). The registers that held the destroyed devices are not cleared, so where no new first or second device is built, the destroyed one is the one passed on: the first gets Joystick_LoadCalibration (0004ae0c)(data\joy1.cal through Path_ApplyAltDrive (000592a4)) and InputDevice_Enable (0004b1c0) on its +0x78, the second the same with joy2.cal as given. Then stores the applied copy. When option 11 (000bd56d) differs from the panel's +0x3a0 and there is a mouse device (Input_GetMouseDevice_Thunk (0004c634)), enables or disables its +0x3a by +0x3a0. Last, Prefs_SaveSelectedOptions (0004ab6c) with ControlsPanel_SaveList (00095348), options 7, 8, 10, 9 and 11. es2_xref finds three calls, from ControlsPanel_Run (00048810), two, and ControlsPanel_Revert (0004903c).

entries.name: ControlsPanel_Revert
entries.description: (panel): Prefs_RevertOption (0004aacc)(1, n) for options 7, 8, 10, 9 and 11; copies option 7 to +0x39c and +0x39d, option 10 to +0x39e, option 9 to +0x39f and option 11 to +0x3a0; then ControlsPanel_ApplyDevices (00048e98). No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: HeapPtr_DtorObjectivesPanelCopy
entries.description: (p, flags), callee-cleaned: the code of HeapPtr_DtorPanelCopy (0002acdc): with p non-null deletes the block p points at with Mem_Delete (000015f8) when that is non-null, then p itself when bit 0 of flags is set. The first function of the objectives panel's object file, a lone copy with no run of ConfigPart's copies after it. es2_xref finds no branch or stored pointer to it.

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_Ctor
entries.description: (panel, rect, keepsScreen) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: the F11 objectives panel. Allocates 0x39e bytes with Mem_New when panel is null (returning 0 when that fails); a 315 x 109 rect, centred by AlertPanel_CenterRect (0004679c) or placed at the rect's point by AlertPanel_SetRect (0004675c); AlertPanel_CtorBase (00045988)(panel, that rect, keepsScreen); StringTable_Ctor (00044f14) on a second string table at +0x318; ObjectiveAlertVtable (000955d6) at +0x314; the plate, frame 0 of dba\hst_alrt loaded with ClassItem_LoadFromFile (0005760c), at +0x2c; str\obj_alrt into +0x30 with StringTable_LoadFromFile (00044f78) and its two one-string groups with StringTable_LoadGroup (000450b0), the title at +0x328 and the button caption at +0x32c; data\object.str, prefixed by Path_ApplyAltDrive (000592a4), into the table +0x318, its group 0 into the pointers from +0x330 and the group's count, StringTable_LoadGroup's answer, as an int16 at +0x380; the title label at +0x40 in WidgetFont_Green6x8 on ((315 - w) >> 1, 3)-(that + w, 13), w the title's width by HudFont_MeasureString (00069d0c), margin (0, -1), with all four words of the title bar +0x2ba set to -20; PanelButton_Ctor (000467c8)(0, 0, panel, (127, 93)-(187, 103)), its caption label in WidgetFont_Cpylw placed by Label_SetRect (00031080) with flags 2 and margin (0, -1), Widget_RegisterClickable (000443d4) with the panel's root +0x281, and widget 0; seven line labels at +0x382 in WidgetFont_Cpylw, placed with flags 1 and margin 0 on (20, 17 + 10i)-(200, 27 + 10i); the cancel widget +0x2e3 = 0. Returns the panel. es2_xref finds one call, from CockpitWidgets_HandleCommand, passing (0, 0, 1). ES2's ObjectivesPanel_Ctor (DBSIM 0045751c), which lists block 13's mission.str lines.

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_Dtor
entries.description: (panel, flags) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: the objectives panel's destructor. Returns at once for a null panel; stores ObjectiveAlertVtable (000955d6) at +0x314, frees the seven line labels at +0x382 with Mem_Delete (000015f8), runs OwnedArray_Dtor (00044f48)(+0x318, 2) and Alert_Dtor (00045d0c)(panel, 0), and frees the panel when bit 0 of flags is set. ObjectiveAlertVtable's +0x1c is 0, and es2_xref finds no branch, stored pointer or slot holding this function or its padding 0004a47d. ES2's ObjectivesPanel_Dtor (DBSIM 00457a80).

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_RunModal

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_Paint

Bitmap_Blit (00067048) of the plate +0x2c with flags 0 at the region's rect +0x18; the title through the panel's slot +8 with +0x328; then each of the +0x380 (int16) string pointers from +0x330 that is not empty goes to the next of the seven line labels at +0x382 with Label_SetText (0003114c), stopping once seven are set; then slot +4 of each widget's +0x1c table. ES2's ObjectivesPanel_Paint (DBSIM 00457b58).

entries.name: ObjectivesPanel_OnChildClick

Sets the close byte +0x2b9 to 1 when child is widget 0 of the +0x2b5 widgets at +0x28d, so ObjectivesPanel_RunModal (0004a4ec) answers 1. entries.name: Prefs_ClearHandlersAndInit
entries.description: No arguments: zeroes the 17 dwords of Prefs_HandlerTable (000bd598) and runs Prefs_Init (0004afe8). es2_xref finds one call, from Input_BuildSourceTable (0004c95c).

entries.name: Prefs_Load
entries.description: (copy): reads the 17 option bytes of data\prefs.cfg (through Path_ApplyAltDrive (000592a4)) into Prefs_Options (000bd562), zeroing them when the file does not open; then for each option calls its handler from the table Prefs_HandlerTable (000bd598) with the value when one is set, copies the value to Prefs_LoadedOptions (000bd574) when copy is non-zero, and copies Prefs_LoadedOptions (000bd574)'s byte to Prefs_PreviousOptions (000bd586).

entries.name: Prefs_CommitOptions
entries.description: (apply): for each of the 17 options, where Prefs_Options (000bd562) differs from the load-time copy Prefs_LoadedOptions (000bd574), calls the option's handler from Prefs_HandlerTable (000bd598) with the value when apply is set and copies the value to the load-time copy; and copies every value to Prefs_PreviousOptions (000bd586). ES2's Prefs_CommitOptions (DBSIM 00459878) over 0x36 options.

entries.name: Prefs_UndoSetOption
entries.description: (index), frameless, its argument removed by this function (RET 4): Prefs_Options (000bd562)[index] = Prefs_PreviousOptions (000bd586)[index], the value before the option's last write; the body is a MOVSX, two byte moves and the RET, with no call, so the option's handler stays unrun. It starts after three 0x90 bytes that follow the RET 4 of 0004a8a8. ES2's Prefs_UndoSetOption (DBSIM 00459924). es2_xref finds one call, from Prefs_LimitDetailInLowMemory (0004adb0).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM capstone disassembly at 0004a900, against ES2's Prefs_UndoSetOption

entries.name: Prefs_SetOption
entries.description: (apply, value, index) in stack order, callee-cleaned: writes one option: saves the old byte at Prefs_PreviousOptions (000bd586)[index], stores value at Prefs_Options (000bd562)[index], and when apply is non-zero and the handler Prefs_HandlerTable (000bd598)[index] is set calls it with value. ES2's Prefs_SetOption (DBSIM 0045993c).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 0004a914, against ES2's Prefs_SetOption

entries.name: Prefs_ToggleOption
entries.description: (apply, index) in stack order, callee-cleaned: saves Prefs_Options (000bd562)[index] at Prefs_PreviousOptions (000bd586)[index], then Prefs_SetOption(apply, value ^ 1, index); returns the new value. ES2's Prefs_ToggleOption (DBSIM 00459980).

entries.name: Prefs_StepOption
entries.description: (apply, modulus, index) in stack order, callee-cleaned: saves Prefs_Options (000bd562)[index] at Prefs_PreviousOptions (000bd586)[index], steps it forward, wrapping to 0 when it reaches modulus, and hands it to Prefs_SetOption(apply, value, index); returns the new value. ES2's Prefs_StepOption (DBSIM 004599b8).

entries.name: Prefs_StepOptionBack
entries.description: (apply, modulus, index) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: saves Prefs_Options (000bd562)[index] at Prefs_PreviousOptions (000bd586)[index], takes 1 from it, giving modulus - 1 below 0, and hands it to Prefs_SetOption (0004a914)(apply, value, index). ES2's Prefs_StepOptionBack (DBSIM 004599f4).

entries.name: Prefs_IncreaseOption
entries.description: (apply, amount, index) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: saves Prefs_Options (000bd562)[index] at Prefs_PreviousOptions (000bd586)[index]; the new value is 0 when it is 0xff, 0xff when adding amount would pass 0xff, and the value plus amount otherwise; Prefs_SetOption (0004a914)(apply, that, index). ES2's Prefs_IncreaseOption (DBSIM 00459a34).

entries.name: Prefs_DecreaseOption
entries.description: (apply, amount, index) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: saves Prefs_Options (000bd562)[index] at Prefs_PreviousOptions (000bd586)[index]; the new value is 0xff when it is 0, 0 when it is below amount, and the value less amount otherwise; Prefs_SetOption (0004a914)(apply, that, index). ES2's Prefs_DecreaseOption (DBSIM 00459a90).

entries.name: Prefs_RevertOption
entries.description: (apply, index) in stack order, callee-cleaned: Prefs_SetOption(apply, Prefs_LoadedOptions (000bd574)[index], index), the shadow value, and returns it. ES2's Prefs_RevertOption (DBSIM 00459ad8).

entries.description: (indices, count) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: for each of count int16 indices, copies Prefs_LoadedOptions (000bd574)[index] over Prefs_Options (000bd562)[index], calling no handler. es2_xref finds calls from Prefs_Init (0004afe8) and PreferencesPanel_Revert (000483d4). ES2's Prefs_RevertSelectedOptions (DBSIM 00459b04).

entries.description: (indices, count) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: reads the 17 bytes of data\prefs.cfg (through Path_ApplyAltDrive (000592a4)) into a buffer with FileRStream_Ctor (000655d0) and FileRStream_Read (0006584c), copies the options the count int16 indices name from Prefs_Options (000bd562) over it, or takes all 17 from Prefs_Options when the file does not open; writes the buffer back with FileWStream_Ctor (0006594c) and FileWStream_Write (00065bbc) when that opens. ES2's Prefs_SaveSelectedOptions (DBSIM 00459b78) over 0x36 bytes.

entries.name: Prefs_OptionChanged
entries.description: (index): whether Prefs_Options (000bd562)[index] differs from the load-time copy Prefs_LoadedOptions (000bd574)[index]. ES2's Prefs_OptionChanged (DBSIM 00459c38).

entries.name: Prefs_SetHandler
entries.description: (handler, option) in stack order, frameless, its arguments removed by this function: stores the handler in the table Prefs_HandlerTable (000bd598) at the option's index, the handler Prefs_SetOption (0004a914) and Prefs_Load (0004a744) call with the option's value.

entries.description: (p, flags), its arguments removed by this function: byte for byte the code of HeapPtr_DtorAppInputCopy (0004c650), relocated operands aside. Opens the object file of the input devices.

entries.description: (part, flags), its arguments removed by this function: slot +0x1c of the vtable 0009565a: byte for byte the code of ConfigPart_DtorAppInputCopy (0004c678), relocated operands aside, storing 0009565a and 0009568e.

entries.description: Frameless: a NOP, then XOR EAX,EAX and RET 4: returns 0. Slot +4 of the vtable 0009565a; the code of ConfigPart_GetClassTagAppInputCopy (0004c6b7).

entries.name: Prefs_ApplySoundsOption
entries.description: (value), the handler Prefs_Init (0004afe8) registers for option 1: calls Sound_SetEffectsEnabled (0004e2c8)(value).

entries.description: (value), the handler Prefs_Init (0004afe8) registers for option 0: calls Sound_SetMusicEnabled (0004e294)(value), then Music_Tick (000585dc) when the value is not 0 and PrefsInitInProgress (000b1734) is clear.
