entries.name: DVJoystick_DetectOnStack
entries.description: No arguments: reserves a 0x78-byte joystick object on the stack, uninitialised, passes it to DVJoystick_Detect (0006be74) and returns that function's answer, left in EAX. The detection reads the object's port word +0x6d, which this function leaves as the stack held it. ES2's DVJoystick_NoOp (VSHELL 00405739) is the Windows build's copy, whose detection stub returns 0. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: DVJoystick_Ctor
entries.description: DVJoystick constructor, (this, mask, port, kind) in stack order, callee-cleaned: allocates 0x78 bytes through Mem_New (000015a4) for a null this, runs GL_ClaimGlobal (0007d5bc)(this, this, kind), and when GL slot kind (000bdd0c + kind * 4) holds this runs DVJoystick_Init (0006b4bc)(this, mask, port, kind); returns this. ES2's DVJoystick_Ctor (VSHELL 0040574d) less its assert for a slot already taken. es2_xref finds one call, from JoystickDevice_Ctor (0004b6c0).

entries.name: DVJoystick_Dtor
entries.description: DVJoystick destructor, (this, flags), callee-cleaned: returns for a null this; when GL slot +0x68 (000bdd0c + index * 4) is non-zero, runs DVJoystick_Shutdown (0006b604) through the 0x90 byte before it and clears the slot, without comparing it with this; then Mem_Delete (000015f8) for flags bit 0. ES2's DVJoystick_Dtor (VSHELL 004057b8) less its assert. es2_xref finds one call, from JoystickDevice_Dtor (0004b7a8).

entries.name: DVJoystick_Init
entries.description: (this, mask, port, kind) in stack order, callee-cleaned: stores kind at +0x68 and the word port at +0x6d; clears +0x25, +0x14, the word +0x66 and +0x77; for each of the four axes zeroes +0x15 and +4 and sets min +0x26 and the band's low edge +0x46 to 0x7fffffff, max +0x36 and the band's high edge +0x56 to 0x80000000. Then DVJoystick_Detect (0006be74): 0 returns 0 with +0 untouched. A mask of 0xf takes the detected mask byte +0x6f; +0x6f is ANDed with the mask, and when the result is 0 or differs from the mask the dword +0 is cleared and 0 returned; otherwise +0x73 = the number of bits set in +0x6f's low four, bit 0 of +0 set, and 1 returned. ES2's DVJoystick_Init (VSHELL 00405823) with the game-port detection where that one calls joyGetDevCapsA.

entries.name: DVJoystick_Shutdown
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: clears bit 0 of the byte +0. ES2's DVJoystick_Shutdown (VSHELL 0040591c). DVJoystick_Dtor (0006b470) calls it through the 0x90 byte at 0006b603.

entries.name: DVJoystick_Poll
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: when bit 0 of +0 is set, DVJoystick_ReadRaw (0006be9f)(this) and then DVJoystick_ReadButtons (0006bf10)(this). The counterpart of ES2's DVJoystick_PollButtons (VSHELL 00405927), which polls through joyGetPos. es2_xref finds two calls, both from Input_PollJoysticks (0004bd90).

entries.name: DVJoystick_ReadAxes
entries.description: (this, out), callee-cleaned: returns 0 when bit 0 of +0 is clear. Otherwise, for each axis i whose bit is set in the mask +0x6f, takes v = the raw count +4[i] held to at most max +0x36[i] (it first stores the count held to at least min +0x26[i], then overwrites that with the count held to the max, so a reading under min passes); then with the shift s = the word +0x66, lo = +0x46[i] and hi = +0x56[i]: below lo, ((v - lo) << s) / (lo - min); above hi, ((v - hi) << s) / (max - hi); otherwise 0; a zero divisor gives 0, IDIV truncates toward zero. Each result goes to +0x15[i]; then the 17 bytes +0x15 to +0x25 (four dwords, the button byte) are copied to out and AL = 1 returned. ES2's DVJoystick_ReadAxes (VSHELL 004059fa) maps Windows' range instead.

entries.name: DVJoystick_ReadAxesDigital
entries.description: (this, out), callee-cleaned: returns 0 when bit 0 of +0 is clear. Otherwise, for all four axes whatever the mask, +0x15[i] = -1 when the raw count +4[i] is below the band's low edge +0x46[i], 1 when above its high edge +0x56[i], else 0; copies the 17 bytes +0x15 to +0x25 to out and returns AL = 1. ES2's DVJoystick_ReadAxesDigital (VSHELL 00405a63) gives 1 or 0 from Windows' position instead.

entries.name: DVJoystick_SetRanges
entries.description: (this, src), callee-cleaned: when bit 0 of +0 is set and src is non-null, memmove (00060998)(this + 0x26, src, 0x40), the calibration block. ES2's DVJoystick_SetRanges (VSHELL 00405ac7). es2_xref finds calls from 00049a7c, 00049f30, 0004a0e8 and Joystick_LoadCalibration (0004ae0c).

entries.name: DVJoystick_GetRanges
entries.description: (this, dst), callee-cleaned: when bit 0 of +0 is set and dst is non-null, memmove (00060998)(dst, this + 0x26, 0x40). ES2's DVJoystick_GetRanges (VSHELL 00405aea). es2_xref finds calls from 00049bbc, 00049f30 and Joystick_SaveCalibration (0004ae90).

entries.name: DVJoystick_TrackRange
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: when bit 0 of +0 is set, DVJoystick_ReadRaw (0006be9f), then for all four axes whatever the mask lowers min +0x26[i] to the raw count +4[i] when the count is below it and raises max +0x36[i] to the count when above. ES2's DVJoystick_TrackRange (VSHELL 00405b0d). es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: DVJoystick_TrackMax
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: DVJoystick_TrackRange (0006b8b8) for the maxima +0x36 alone. ES2's DVJoystick_TrackMax (VSHELL 00405b5d). es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: DVJoystick_TrackMin
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: DVJoystick_TrackRange (0006b8b8) for the minima +0x26 alone. ES2's DVJoystick_TrackMin (VSHELL 00405b93). es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: DVJoystick_TrackRange2
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: DVJoystick_TrackRange (0006b8b8) on the center band, lowering its low edge +0x46[i] and raising its high edge +0x56[i] to each raw count outside them. ES2's VSHELL DVJoystick_TrackRange2 (00405bc9). es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: DVJoystick_WaitForFlag
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: saves the button-read delay +0x77, sets it to 0x80, calls DVJoystick_ReadButtons (0006bf10) until the button byte +0x14 is non-zero, then restores +0x77. ES2's DVJoystick_WaitForFlag (VSHELL 00405c19). es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: DVJoystick_WaitForFlagClear
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: DVJoystick_WaitForFlag (0006bb2c) waiting for the button byte +0x14 to be 0. ES2's DVJoystick_WaitForFlagClear (VSHELL 00405c48). es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: DVJoystick_ReadFlag
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: DVJoystick_ReadButtons (0006bf10), then returns the button byte +0x14 in AL. ES2's DVJoystick_ReadFlag (VSHELL 00405c77). es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: Mouse_DetectThunk
entries.description: A frameless stub, without arguments: calls Mouse_Detect (00055978) and returns its answer. The first code of the mouse driver object's file, after the joystick class's file and its two zero bytes. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: DVMouse_Ctor
entries.description: (mouse) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: allocates 0x3a bytes when mouse is null, returning 0 when that fails; GL_ClaimGlobal (0007d5bc)(mouse, mouse, 2); the inlined constructors of +4, +0xe and +0x24; when the GL slot 2 (000bdd14) holds the mouse and DVMouse_Init (0006bd10) answers non-zero, atexit (0007d628)(Mouse_ResetThunk (00055c47)) and Assert_AddHook (0005730c)(DVMouse_AssertHook (0006bccc)); returns the mouse. VSHELL's DVMouse_Ctor (004052fb), which asserts when the slot is taken and registers no exit routine. es2_xref finds one call, from MouseInputDevice_Ctor (0004c1e0).

entries.name: DVMouse_AssertHook
entries.description: Frameless: CALL Mouse_Reset (00055a67), then RET 4; Ghidra has no function there. DVMouse_Ctor (0006bbc8) registers it with Assert_AddHook, where VSHELL's registers the empty DVMouse_AssertHookNoOp (0040550a).

entries.name: DVMouse_Dtor
entries.description: (mouse, flags) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function: for a mouse that is set, when the GL slot 2 (000bdd14) is set, runs DVMouse_Shutdown (0006bd84)(mouse) by its padding 0006bd81 and clears the slot; frees the mouse with Mem_Delete when bit 0 of flags is set. VSHELL's DVMouse_Dtor (0040535f), which asserts when the slot is clear. es2_xref finds one call, from MouseInputDevice_Dtor (0004c220).

entries.name: DVMouse_Init
entries.description: (mouse) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function, entered also at its padding 0006bd0e: Mouse_Install (000559c9)(mouse, mouse + 4); when bit 0 of the dword +0 is then set, Mouse_SetDoubleX (00055aa4)(1), MouseDriver_GetBounds (0006bdbc)(mouse, mouse + 0x24), the dwords +0xe, +0x12, +0x16 and +0x1a set to 0, 0, 320 and 200, MouseDriver_GetBounds (0006bdbc)(mouse, mouse + 0xe) and MouseDriver_SetBounds (0006bdf0)(mouse, mouse + 0xe). Returns bit 0 of +0. VSHELL's DVMouse_Init (004053bf), which installs no driver, calls an empty function in place of Mouse_SetDoubleX and sets the bounds to 0, 0, 480 and 640. es2_xref finds one call, from DVMouse_Ctor (0006bbc8).

entries.name: DVMouse_Shutdown
entries.description: (mouse) in stack order, its arguments removed by this function, entered also at its padding 0006bd81: when bit 0 of the dword +0 is set, zeroes that dword and calls Mouse_Reset (00055a67); when that answers non-zero, MouseDriver_SetBounds (0006bdf0)(mouse, mouse + 0x24) and returns 1. entries.name: DVJoystick_Detect
entries.description: (joystick), C convention, hand-written with an ENTER frame: with ESI = joystick and EAX = 0, DVJoystick_DetectGamePort (0006bf4d); returns 1 when the axis mask +0x6f is then non-zero. Otherwise DVJoystick_DetectBios (0006bfc2), returning 1 when +0x6f is non-zero and 0 when it is 0. The counterpart of ES2's DVJoystick_ReturnZero (VSHELL 00405724).

entries.name: DVJoystick_ReadRaw
entries.description: (joystick), C convention, hand-written, keeping every register: with the BIOS byte +0x6c at 1, DVJoystick_ReadRawBios (0006c038). Otherwise, with interrupts off: writes the port word +0x6d (OUT), reads it until every bit of the axis mask +0x6f reads 1, up to 0x10000 reads, returning with nothing stored when they run out; then reads it with a fresh count of 0x10000 shared by all axes, and at each read where masked bits have dropped pushes the bits and the count left. Interrupts back on, it stores for each pushed group, at +4 + bit * 4 of each bit, the number of reads since the second count began less 1, until +0x73 axes are stored. When the second count runs out first, it pops its saved registers as groups and restores registers from the wrong stack slots. The counterpart of ES2's DVJoystick_ReadRawNoOp (VSHELL 0040572b).

entries.name: DVJoystick_ReadButtons
entries.description: (joystick), C convention, hand-written, keeping every register but ECX: when the delay byte +0x77 is non-zero, first runs a LOOP of +0x77 * 256 iterations; then with the BIOS byte +0x6c at 1, DVJoystick_ReadButtonsBios (0006c05f); otherwise, with interrupts off, reads the port word +0x6d and stores its inverted high four bits, moved to bits 0-3, in +0x14 and +0x25. The counterpart of ES2's DVJoystick_PollNoOp (VSHELL 00405732).

entries.name: DVJoystick_DetectGamePort
entries.description: Hand-written, frameless, taking the joystick in ESI and keeping EAX to EDX: with interrupts off, clears the axis mask +0x6f and its count +0x73, writes the port word +0x6d (OUT), and reads it until bits 0-3 all read 1, up to 0x10000 reads, returning when they run out. Then reads it with a fresh count of 0x10000: bits that drop within 0xfa0 (4000) reads of that count's start are ORed into +0x6f and counted into +0x73, later drops are passed over, until all four have dropped or the count runs out; interrupts back on.

entries.name: DVJoystick_DetectBios
entries.description: Hand-written, frameless, taking the joystick in ESI and keeping EAX to EDX: INT 15h with AX 8404h, DX 1 and EBX loaded from DVJoystick_BiosDriverEbx (0009b698); returns on carry. Otherwise sets mask bit 0 when AX is non-zero and at most 0xfa0, bit 1 for BX, bit 2 when CX is non-zero and BX at most 0xfa0 (the limit is tested on BX), and bit 3 for DX, counting each into +0x73, and sets the BIOS byte +0x6c to 1 when +0x73 is non-zero.

entries.name: DVJoystick_ReadRawBios
entries.description: Hand-written, frameless, taking the joystick in ESI and keeping EAX to EDX: INT 15h with AX 8400h, DX 1 and EBX loaded from DVJoystick_BiosDriverEbx (0009b698), storing the returned EAX, EBX, ECX and EDX whole in the four raw axes +4, +8, +0xc and +0x10, whatever the mask.

entries.name: DVJoystick_ReadButtonsBios
entries.description: Hand-written, frameless, taking the joystick in ESI and keeping EAX, EBX and EDX: INT 15h with AX 8400h, DX 0 and EBX loaded from DVJoystick_BiosDriverEbx (0009b698), storing AL inverted and shifted right by 4 in the button bytes +0x14 and +0x25.

entries.description: (mode), C convention: returns 0 with no Keyboard_Instance (0009b6aa). entries.description: (divisor, timer), C convention: when Pit_Timer (0009bd40) is already set, clears the timer's +0 and returns 0. Otherwise clears both callback masks (Timer_CallbackMask (0009cd64), Timer_DelayedMask (0009cd68)), keeps DS in 0009bd54 and 0009bd58, saves interrupt 8's protected-mode vector (INT 21h AX=2502h) at 0009bd48/0009bd4c and its real-mode vector (AX=2503h) at 0009bd4e, sets Pit_Timer to the timer, and Pit_SetDivisor (0006d18c)(divisor); when that answers, installs Pit_TimerInterrupt (0006d391) for interrupt 8 with INT 21h AX=2506h (gaining control in protected mode in either mode), sets bit 0 of the timer's +0 and returns EAX as the call leaves it.

entries.name: Pit_TimerInterrupt
entries.description: Interrupt 8's handler, which Pit_InstallHandler (0006d1c2) installs: saves every register, loads DS and ES from 0009bd54, and sends the interrupt controller its end of interrupt (0x20 to port 0x20). While Pit_InHandler (0009bd52) is set it returns at once. Otherwise it counts itself in, enables interrupts, switches to the stack whose top is Pit_Countdown (0009cd5c) (selector 0009bd58), takes 1 off Pit_Countdown (0009cd5c) while it is above 0 and adds 1 to Pit_InterruptCount (0009cd60); for each set bit of Timer_CallbackMask (0009cd64), lowest first, takes 1 off the counter 0009cdec and at 0 calls the callback 0009cd6c and reloads the counter from 0009ce6c; for each set bit of Timer_DelayedMask (0009cd68), takes 1 off the delay 0009ceec while it is not 0 and otherwise off the counter 0009ce2c, and at 0 calls the callback 0009cdac and takes 1 off the repeats 0009cf2c, clearing the slot's bit when they reach 0 and reloading the counter from 0009ceac when not. Stores the rate, lowers the divisor 0009d7dc to 0x1234dc / rate when that is smaller, works out every live event's step as HmiTimer_AddEvent (0006d5e6) does and zeroes its accumulator. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiTimer_RemoveEvent
entries.description: (event) of the HMI library: clears the event's far handler, sets the divisor through HmiTimer_SetDivisor (0006da37) to 0x1234dc / the highest rate among the live events whose rate is not 0xff00, or to 0xffff with none, then works out every live event's step as HmiTimer_AddEvent (0006d5e6) does and zeroes its accumulator. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiTimer_GetEventRate
entries.description: (event) of the HMI library: returns the event's rate from 0009d840.

entries.name: HmiTimer_SetDivisor
entries.description: (divisor) of the HMI library: stores it at 0009d7dc and calls HmiTimer_NoOp with it.

entries.name: HmiTimer_Dispatch
entries.description: Far function of the HMI library: for each of the 16 timer events with a non-null far handler at 0009d7e0, adds the event's step 0009d880 to its accumulator 0009d8c0 and, when bit 16 of the accumulator is set, clears the accumulator's high word, stores the event's byte of 0009d900 in 0009d910 unless it is 0xff, and far-calls the handler. The loop index is the dword 0009db28. RETF.

entries.name: HmiDigi_StartSample
entries.description: (driver, block) of the HMI library: returns 0 when the dword 0009d0d8[driver] is above 0xe105, and -1 when all 32 voices (far pointers at 0009d10c + driver*0xc0) have bit 0x8000 of their word +0x30 set. Otherwise fills the first free voice from the block: the data far pointer at +0 and +8 and data + block +0x30 at +0x10; with block flags (+0x28) bit 0x40 clear the length block +8 at +0x18 and +0x1c, set block +0x30 there, +0x34 at +0x20 and block +0x2c less both at +0x2c; the words block +0x14 at +0x32, +0x18 at +0x34, the flags | 0xa000 at +0x30, +0x10 at +0x36, +0xc at +0x38, +0x24 at +0x4a; the far callback block +0x1c at +0x3c, +0x38 at +0x44, the length at +0x50, the words of +0x40-+0x58 at +0x54-+0x60; zeroes +0x3a, +0x48, +0x4c, +0x64 and +0x68. Returns the voice's number.

entries.name: HmiDigi_StopSample
entries.description: (driver, voice), C convention: 10 for a voice above 31; for a voice record (the far pointer at 0009d10c + driver * 0xc0 + voice * 6) whose word +0x30 has bit 0x8000 set and bit 0x1000 clear, clears bit 0x8000 (the byte +0x31 & 0x7f) and the word +0x34; answers 0 either way, so a busy voice with bit 0x1000 set is not stopped. es2_xref finds calls from DigiSound_Stop (00050c88), maybe_DigiSound_Pause (000509a0) and HmiDigiMidi_SendEvent (00081789).

entries.name: HmiDigi_IsVoiceDone
entries.description: (driver, voice), C convention: 10 for a voice above 31; 1 when bit 0x8000 of the voice record's word +0x30 (the far pointer at 0009d10c + driver * 0xc0 + voice * 6) is clear, 0 while it is set. es2_xref finds one call, from DigiSound_IsPlaying (00050c18), which answers whether it is 0.

entries.name: HmiDigi_CountBusyVoices
entries.description: (driver), C convention: how many of the driver's 32 voice records (the far pointers at 0009d10c + driver * 0xc0 + voice * 6) have bit 0x8000 of their word +0x30 set, the busy voices. es2_xref finds one call, from DigiSound_Play (000509c4), which makes room above 30.

entries.name: HmiDigi_SetSampleVolume
entries.description: (driver, voice, volume), C convention: with bit 0x8000 of the voice record's word +0x30 set (the far pointer at 0009d10c + driver * 0xc0 + voice * 6), stores the volume in its word +0x32 and answers the old word; else answers 0. It does not test the voice's range. es2_xref finds calls from DigiSound_SetPlacedVolume (00050954), DigiSound_SetVolume (000508c4) and HmiDigiMidi_SendEvent (00081789).

entries.name: HmiDigi_SetSamplePan
entries.description: (driver, voice, pan), C convention: with bit 0x8000 of the voice record's word +0x30 set (the far pointer at 0009d10c + driver * 0xc0 + voice * 6), stores the pan in its word +0x54, where HmiDigi_StartSample (0006dad9) puts the start block's +0x40, and answers the old word; else answers 0. It does not test the voice's range. es2_xref finds one call, from HmiDigiMidi_SendEvent (00081789).

entries.name: HmiMidi_InitSong
entries.description: (song block, track map, handle out) of the HMI library, the .HMP loader: returns 0xe when the file the block's far pointer gives does not open HMIMIDIP and 0xb when all 8 song slots (far pointers at 000a22ec) are taken. Keeps the file and the track map in the slot, the track count +0x30 at 000a2178 and 000a2198, and writes the block's callback into the file at +0x300 (offset) and +0x304 (selector); clears the slot's 127 entries at 000a5fec and two far pointers. Walks the tracks from +0x308, each chunk +4 bytes on: keeps the chunk's pointer, and its events pointer (chunk +0xc) moved past the first delta HmiMidi_ReadDelta (0006ed60) reads into 000a1948[track]. From the branch table at the file's +0x20 offset (a count byte per track, then 24-byte entries) keeps each track's first entry and writes each entry's file + [+0xc] at +8. Then routes each track whose map entry is 0xff to the first open driver (ids at 000a130c, 5) that answers one of its device ids at +0x80 + track*0x14 (5, ending at 0): 0xa000 answered by 0xa000, 0xa001 or 0xa008, 0xa002 by 0xa002 or 0xa009, others by themselves; a first id of 0 maps to 0, and a track nothing answers loses its events pointer, maps to 0xff and decrements 000a2178. Returns 0 with the slot through the handle pointer. es2_xref finds one call, from MidiSound_Play (00050652).

entries.name: HmiMidi_FreeSong
entries.description: (song) of the HMI library: 10 for a song of 8 or more; otherwise clears the song's file far pointer at 000a22ec and returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_StartSong
entries.description: (song) of the HMI library: registers the far pointer CS:HmiMidi_SongTick (0007ef95) with HmiTimer_AddEvent (0006d5e6) at the rate the song file's +0x38 holds, the event's number going to 000a24e8[song], and returns a non-zero result. Otherwise stores the song in 0009d900[event], sets the playing flag 000a22ac[song] and returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_StopSong
entries.description: (song) of the HMI library: 10 for a song of 8 or more. Removes the song's timer event with HmiTimer_RemoveEvent (0006d8d5) unless its number is -1, sets 0009d900[event] to 0xff and the number to -1. While the playing flag 000a22ac[song] is set it calls HmiMidi_SilenceSong (00071f84), clears the flag and the song's file far pointer, and calls HmiMidi_ResetSong (0006eb98) with a block of the file's far pointer and the callback from the file's +0x300. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_ResetSong
entries.description: (song, block) of the HMI library: puts a song back at its start as HmiMidi_InitSong (0006e4c1) sets it up. Stores the block's file far pointer at 000a22ec[song], the file's track count +0x30 at 000a2178 and 000a2198, and the block's callback into the file's +0x300 and +0x304. For each track from +0x308 zeroes its tick count 000a1d48, keeps the chunk's far pointer (000a3fd8) and the events pointer (000a1348) moved past the first delta, which HmiMidi_ReadDelta (0006ed60) reads into 000a1948. Then clears the events pointer of each track whose track map entry is 0xff and takes 1 off 000a2178 for it. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_ReadDelta
entries.description: (bytes, far out pointer) of the HMI library: reads a variable-length number, seven bits a byte with the first byte the lowest, ending at the byte whose bit 7 is set; stores it through the out pointer and returns the number of bytes read.

entries.name: HmiMidi_SetMasterVolume
entries.description: (volume) of the HMI library: stores the byte at 000a56d8 and, for each open driver (ids at 000a130c up to a 0) and each of 16 channels the driver's table at 000a5688 marks, and channel 9, calls the driver entry's first function (000a21b8 + slot*0x24) with the 3-byte controller 7 event at 000a55c8 whose value is the channel's kept volume 000a56fc * volume >> 7, or 0 while the channel's flag at 000a785c is set. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_SetLoopCallback
entries.description: (song, far callback) of the HMI library: stores the callback at 000a5fbc + song*6, which HmiMidi_SongTick (0007ef95) calls at a loop end controller. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_SetBranchCallback
entries.description: (song, far callback) of the HMI library: stores the callback at 000a5f8c + song*6, which HmiMidi_SongTick (0007ef95) calls at a branch controller. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_SetTriggerCallback
entries.description: (song, index, far callback) of the HMI library: stores the callback at 000a5fec + song*0x2fa + index*6, which HmiMidi_SongTick (0007ef95) calls at a controller 0x77 of that value. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_BranchTrack
entries.description: (song, track, id) of the HMI library: finds the track's branch entry whose byte +4 is the id, walking the 24-byte entries from the track's first (000a598c) with no bound, sets the track's events pointer to the chunk + the entry's +0 + 0xc, sends each pair of the entry's data (+7 bytes at the pointer +8) as a controller on the chunk's +8 channel through HmiMidi_SendEvent (000715c5), clears the byte 000a77bc and returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_BranchSong
entries.description: (song, id) of the HMI library: for each track from 1 with an events pointer, finds its branch entry whose byte +4 is the id with bit 0x80 set, sets the events pointer to the chunk + the entry's +0 + 0xc and past the delta there, which HmiMidi_ReadDelta (0006ed60) reads into the track's delta, zeroes the track's tick count and sends each pair of the entry's data as a controller on the channel of the event landed on through HmiMidi_SendEvent (000715c5). Clears the byte 000a77bc and returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_IsSongDone
entries.description: (song) of the HMI library: 1 when the playing flag 000a22ac[song] is 0, else 0.

entries.name: HmiLib_ErrorText
entries.description: (error) of the HMI library: returns the string pointer at 0009dd2c + error*4.

entries.name: HmiMidi_PauseSong
entries.description: (song, silence) of the HMI library: sets the paused flag 000a226c[song], which stops HmiMidi_SongTick (0007ef95) for the song. With silence non-zero, for each of 32 tracks with an events pointer it calls the track's driver's first function with a controller 7 event of value 0 on the chunk's +8 channel (mapped through 000a45d8 in the channel-stealing mode) and sets the channel's flag at 000a785c. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_ResumeSong
entries.description: (song) of the HMI library: clears the paused flag 000a226c[song] and, for each of 32 tracks with an events pointer, sends a controller 7 with the channel's kept volume 000a56fc through HmiMidi_SendEvent (000715c5) and clears the channel's flag at 000a785c. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_MuteSong
entries.description: (song) of the HMI library: sets the muted flag 000a228c[song] and, for each of 32 tracks with an events pointer, calls the track's driver's first function with a controller 7 event of value 0 on the chunk's +8 channel. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_UnmuteSong
entries.description: (song) of the HMI library: clears the muted flag 000a228c[song] and, for each of 32 tracks with an events pointer, sends a controller 7 with the channel's kept volume 000a56fc through HmiMidi_SendEvent (000715c5). Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_SetSongVolume
entries.description: (song, volume) of the HMI library: stores the byte as the dword 000a56dc[song] and, for each of 32 tracks with an events pointer, calls the track's driver's first function with a controller 7 event on the chunk's +8 channel whose value is the channel's kept volume 000a56fc * volume >> 7. Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_FadeSong
entries.description: (song, flags, time, from, to) of the HMI library: the step count is ((time << 16) / (0x640000 / the rate of the song's timer event, HmiTimer_GetEventRate (0006da29))) >> 2. With a count of 0 it calls HmiMidi_StopSong (0006ead9) for flag 4 and otherwise HmiMidi_SetSongVolume (0006f64e) with to. Otherwise it sets the song volume to from and stores the flags (000a77c0), the step (000a77e0), the difference of the two volumes << 16 over the count, taken as to - from with bit 0 of flags set and from - to without, the volume from << 16 (000a7800) and the count (000a7820), which HmiMidi_SongTick (0007ef95) steps. Returns 0.

entries.name: Str_FindBoyerMoore
entries.description: (text, pattern), C convention: a Boyer-Moore search for pattern in text, comparing from the pattern's end with a 256-entry skip table filled by __memintset; returns the match's address, text itself for an empty pattern, and 0 when there is no match or the pattern is longer than the text.

entries.name: Str_ToLowerInPlace
entries.description: (string), C convention: each byte up to the zero through tolower, in place; returns the string. The sibling of Str_ToUpperInPlace (0006d4b4). es2_xref finds calls from SoundManager_CreateObject (0004f4e8) and SoundManager_SetSampleName (0004f99c), which lower-case a sample name in place with it.

entries.name: HmiDigi_InitSystem
entries.description: (far path) of the HMI library, the digital library's start: sets 0009db40 to 1, copies the path's string to 0009d914, or an empty string for a null pointer, stores DS's absolute address (__dosx_get_abs_address) in 0009db14, calls 0006f971 and returns 0. es2_xref finds two calls, from SoundManager_LoadDrivers (0004ef8c); the one before HmiMidi_InitSystem (00070ed8) passes sos\.

entries.name: HmiDigi_UninitSystem
entries.description: Of the HMI library, the digital library's stop: calls 0006fb96, clears 0009db40, which HmiDigi_InitSystem (0006fdbb) sets, and returns 0.

entries.name: HmiDigi_InitDriver
entries.description: (device, far hardware block, far init block, far handle) of the HMI library, the digital driver's open: takes the first of five driver numbers whose device dword 0009d510 is 0, answering 0xb when there is none, and stores the device there. With the init block's far pointer +0x24 null it loads the driver image with 00080dd1, answering its error, and stores what that gives in the init block's +0x24, +0x2c, +0x44 and +0x54; otherwise it takes those from the block. It answers the error of 000812d1 on the driver's 0x6c-byte record at 0009d528. For a device below 0xe106: with the init block's +0x0c 0 the buffer is the init block's far pointer +0x04; otherwise it allocates the init block's +0x00 bytes with 0007074d, answering 5 when that fails, and fills them with 0x80 when the record's +0x24 is 8 and bit 0x80 of its +0x3d is clear, else with 0. It then calls 000809b8, keeps the far handler that gives at 0009d0ec, and calls 00080715 on the driver's voice pointers (0009d10c + driver * 0xc0); for a device from 0xe106 the handler is 0. It writes the handler into the init block's +0x1c, calls 00080ab8, 00080a0a (with the init block's +0x14 and +0x18), 00080a90, HmiDigi_CallDriver2 (00080a69) with the init block's +0x10, the rate, and 00080a3f with the buffer and its size, sets 0009d040 and 0009d068, copies the blocks' fields into the driver's 0x5c-byte entry at 000a231c (its +0x14 the device), stores the driver number through the handle pointer and returns 0. es2_xref finds one call, from HmiDigiMidi_Open (00081b08).

entries.name: HmiDigi_UninitDriver
entries.description: (driver, free, unload) of the HMI library, the digital driver's close: answers 1 when the driver's open flag 0009d040 is clear. Otherwise it clears 0009d068; when 0009d0d8[driver] is below 0xe106, 0009db2c[driver] is set (the open allocated the buffer) and free is non-zero, it frees the buffer through 00070906 when 00080c1c answers 3 and clears 0009db2c. It then calls 000808d6, 00080994 and 00080aee, and with unload non-zero 00081002 and 0008127a, clears the driver's far pointers, its device 0009d510 and its open flag, and answers 0. es2_xref finds calls from HmiDigiMidi_Close (00081c4b) and SoundManager_UnloadDrivers (0004f3d4).

entries.name: HmiMidi_InitSystem
entries.description: (far path) of the HMI library, the MIDI library's start: copies the path's string to the driver path 000a575c, or an empty string for a null pointer, stores DS's absolute address (__dosx_get_abs_address) in 0009db14, calls 00070985, fills HmiCallbackMidi_Functions (000a2574) with the far pointers of HmiCallbackMidi_SendEvent (00081719), HmiCallbackMidi_Open (00081739), HmiCallbackMidi_Close (00081744), HmiCallbackMidi_Reset (0008174f) and HmiCallbackMidi_SetCallback (0008175a), and HmiDigiMidi_Functions (000a3028) with those of HmiDigiMidi_SendEvent (00081789), HmiDigiMidi_Open (00081b08), HmiDigiMidi_Close (00081c4b), HmiDigiMidi_Reset (00081cb0) and HmiDigiMidi_LoadBank (00081cd3), sets HmiMidi_SystemStarted (000a2570) to 1 and returns 0. es2_xref finds one call, from SoundManager_LoadDrivers (0004ef8c), which passes sos\.

entries.name: HmiMidi_UninitSystem
entries.description: Of the HMI library, the MIDI library's stop: calls 00070c1b, clears HmiMidi_SystemStarted (000a2570) and returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_InitDriver
entries.description: (device, port block, block, handle out) of the HMI library: takes the first of 5 driver slots whose id at 000a130c is 0, returning 0xb with none, stores the device there and copies its 16 bytes from 000a55d8 + (device - 0xa000)*16 to 000a5688. For 0xa005 and 0xa003 copies six far pointers (from HmiDigiMidi_Functions (000a3028) or HmiCallbackMidi_Functions (000a2574)) into the slot's 0x24-byte entry at 000a21b8 and calls its entry +6 with the block's far pointer +0x18/+0x1c, the slot and HmiMidi_DriverArg (000a5984). For any other device loads the driver with HmiMidi_LoadDriverImage (00081365) unless the block's far pointer +4 is set (keeping its results in the block's +4-+0x14 and +0x28), calls HmiMidi_IsDriverSlotFree (000816f5) and HmiDriver_GetFunctions (00081687), and calls the driver's entry +6 with the port block's +8, +4 and +0. A non-zero result is returned; for 0xa00a it also calls HmiTimer_AddEvent (0006d5e6)(0x78, ...). Marks the slot open (000a12e4), stores it through the handle pointer and returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_CloseDriver
entries.description: (slot, free) of the HMI library: 1 when the slot's open flag 000a12e4 is clear. Otherwise calls the driver entry's +0xc function, removes the timer event 000a5988 with HmiTimer_RemoveEvent (0006d8d5) for device 0xa00a, calls HmiMidi_FreeDriverImage (00081599) when free is non-zero and the device is neither 0xa003 nor 0xa005, clears the slot's two far pointers (000a127c, 000a129c), its device id (000a130c) and the open flag, and returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_ResetDriver
entries.description: (slot) of the HMI library: on each of 16 channels calls the driver entry's first function with controller 0x79 and then 0x7b, value 0, then the entry's +0x12 function with the far pointer 000a597c, the slot and HmiMidi_DriverArg (000a5984). Returns 0.

entries.name: HmiMidi_SendEvent
entries.description: (song, far event pointer, driver slot, length) of the HMI library. With the channel-stealing mode 000a55d4 off: a controller event is copied to the 4-byte buffer 000a55c8, a controller 7 with its value kept at 000a56fc[slot*16 + channel] and replaced by ((value * the song volume 000a56dc[song]) >> 7) * the master volume 000a56d8 >> 7, or by 0 while the muted flag 000a228c[song] is set, and the driver entry's first function (000a21b8 + slot*0x24) is called with the buffer, the length and the slot; any other event is passed to that function as it is. Returns 1. With the mode on it maps the event's channel to a device channel through 000a45d8, taking a free one of those the driver's table 000a5688 marks or taking one over by the values at the song file's +0x40, re-sends the kept program, pitch bend, volume and controller 0x40 to a newly taken channel, rewrites the event's channel for the call and restores it after.

entries.name: HmiMidi_SilenceSong
entries.description: (song) of the HMI library: for each track up to the file's count whose track map entry is neither -1 nor 0xff, calls the driver entry's first function four times on the chunk's +8 channel: controller 0x7b value 0, controller 0x79 value 0, the pitch bend bytes 0x40 0x40, and controller 7 value 0. In the channel-stealing mode it uses the mapped channel and frees the mapping. Returns 1.

entries.name: HmiMidi_SetChannelStealing
entries.description: (mode) of the HMI library: stores it at 000a55d4 and returns the old value. es2_xref finds one call, from SoundManager_LoadDrivers.

entries.name: HmiMidi_LoadBank
entries.description: (slot, offset, selector, x) of the HMI library: far-calls the slot's driver entry +0x18 function (000a21b8 + slot * 0x24) with the far pointer selector:offset, the slot and x, and answers what it answers, EAX left as the call returns it. es2_xref finds three calls, from SoundManager_LoadDrivers (0004ef8c).

entries.name: strchr
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `strchr`, from `strings.ASM`: Symantec C++ 6.1's library code for it matches here whole, relocated operands masked, and the search over the image finds it at this address only. The match covers 39 bytes from here.

entries.name: Dongle_Ctor
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: returns this, or a new 1-byte object when this is null.

entries.name: Dongle_Dtor
entries.description: (this, flags), callee-cleaned: deletes this when it is not null and bit 0 of flags is set.

entries.name: Dongle_Check
entries.description: (this), callee-cleaned: calls 00082698(1, 0x13d, 0, 0, 0, four answer pointers), the seed 0x13d and the 0 from the dwords 0009dec0 and 0009dec4, and returns 1 when the first answer is 0; then calls 00082698(2, 0x13d, 0, 0x6fc3, 0x7b7f, four answer pointers), the two passwords from 0009decc and 0009ded0, and returns 0 when the answers are 0xcb57, 0x753c, 0x648e and 0xc042 and 2 otherwise: Dongle_PrintStatus's 'okay', 'Missing' and 'wrong Password'.

entries.name: Raster_FindDriverTable
entries.description: (number in EAX), asm: walks the {number, table} pairs at 0009df68 and returns the table whose number matches, or the first negative number, the list's end: drivers 0 (000a7ae0), 1 (000a7b70) and 3 (000a7c00).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM disassembly at 00073234; image dwords at 0009df68

entries.name: Raster_InstallDriverTable
entries.description: (number), C convention: Raster_FindDriverTable (00073234)(number); for -1 returns 0, otherwise copies the 0009df64 dwords (0x24 in the image) of the table to 0009ded4 with REP MOVSD and returns 1. The copy fills the raster's routine slots (0009df08, 0009df3c, 0009df44, 0009df58 among them), all 0 in the image.

entries.name: RasterDriver_OpenDisplay
entries.description: (driver, bitmap, info), C convention: looks the driver's table up afresh for each call with Raster_FindDriverTable (number in EAX): slot 8 (bitmap) and slot 9 () must each return 0, else returns 0; then slot 10 (), slot 11 (bitmap, info) and slot 7 (info + 0x24, info), and returns 1. ES2's RasterDriver_OpenDisplay (DBSIM 0048930a). GLDisplay_Open passes display + 4 as info.

entries.name: Transform_LocalPointDotNormal
entries.description: (point, transform, normal), C convention: subtracts the transform's int32 translation (+0x14, +0x18, +0x1c) from the int32 point, rotates the difference by the transform's int16 Q14 matrix (+0 to +0x11, each axis rounded with +0x2000 >> 14) and returns its dot product with the int16 normal in EDX:EAX. ES2's Transform_LocalPointDotNormal (DBSIM 004910b4), identical after normalisation.

entries.name: Math_Atan2Bam
entries.description: (x, y), C convention: atan2 as a 16-bit binary angle. The smaller magnitude shifted left 9, plus half the larger, divided by the larger gives a quotient q; q is 0 or q*4 plus the byte table 0009e648[q]. When |y| > |x| the angle is 0x1000 minus that; a negative x makes it 0x2000 minus the angle and a negative y 0x4000 minus it; the result is shifted left 2 and masked to 16 bits. A y of 0 gives 0, or 0x8000 with x negative. ES2's Math_Atan2Bam (DBSIM 0047d220) with its PUSH EBX/POP EBX left out, so EBX is overwritten.

entries.name: Math_Q16Divide
entries.description: (a, b), C convention: Q16 divide rounded to nearest: (|a| << 16) / |b| by DIV, plus 1 when the remainder is at least half of |b| rounded up, then negated when the signs differ. ES2's Math_Q16Divide (DBSIM 0047df5c) truncates.

entries.name: Math_Q16Multiply
entries.description: (a, b), C convention: Q16 multiply rounded to nearest: (int64)a * b + 0x8000, shifted right 16. es2_xref finds 20 calls. ES2's Math_Q16Multiply (DBSIM 0047df81) truncates.

entries.name: Math_Q16Multiply2
entries.description: (a, b), C convention: Math_Q16Multiply's body. es2_xref finds three calls, all from Math_NormalizeVec3ToLength (00063b5c). ES2's Math_Q16Multiply2 (DBSIM 0047df71) truncates.

entries.name: VGA8_SpanBitmapRow
entries.description: (edgeA, edgeB, header, table), C convention: one row (000bd94c) of VGA8_FillBitmapPolygon from edgeA's x +0x1c to edgeB's, both included, n pixels. du = Math_Q16Divide(uB - uA, n << 16), dv likewise; pixel i samples u = uA + (du >> 1) + i * du, v likewise, texel at header +0xa + round(v) * header +2 + round(u) (the 0x8000 add carried into the unsigned high words), stepped exactly in 16.16. Clip mode +0x204 other than 2 clamps to the rect +0x20c..+0x214 columns (skipped pixels advancing u, v by Math_Q16Multiply); mode 2 walks the clip block's region list from the last entry, drawing the row's part in every type-0 rect (+4..+0x10) or type-2 span region holding it, and returns at any other type. Writes the planar display through the sequencer's map mask, ROL-stepping the plane. With table 0 a texel of 0 is not written (OR AH,AH / JZ at 0007390a); otherwise every texel is written as table[texel].

entries.description: ES2's Poly_ScanConvertToSpanRegion (DBSIM 00484614), the scan conversion of a polygon into the span region the span routine fills: es2_naming.py diff finds the two the same after normalisation but for the computed jump into the unrolled stores. ES1's JMP EDX at 0007761a enters the run of stores before 000788dc at 12 bytes a store (EDX = 000788dc - 12 x (n + 1)), each store STOSW, ADD EDI,ECX, ADD [EBP - 0x1b8],EBX and ADC EAX,ESI, so the accumulator steps in the frame; after the run the JMP at 000788dc goes back to 0007709f, and three zero bytes follow it before Poly_ClipToRect (000788e4). ES2's saves EBP at 004a33ec, takes its accumulator into EBP and enters its run before 004865e4 at 8 bytes a store, ADD EBP,EBX in place of the frame add. es2_xref finds four calls, from Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch (00068be0).
entries.source: Herculan/docs/es1/rendering/screen-pages.md#clipped-polygons; es2_naming.py diff ES1DBSIM 00076f54 DBSIM 00484614; ES1DBSIM disassembly at 00077605-0007761a and bytes at 0007761c and 000788c4

entries.name: Poly_ClipToRect
entries.description: ES2's Poly_ClipToRect (DBSIM 0048422c), the clip of a polygon to a rect: es2_naming.py diff finds the two identical after normalisation (260 lines). es2_xref finds three calls, from Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch (00068be0), which clips a span fill with it against the clip block's rect in clip mode 1 and against each rect region in clip mode 2. It opens an object file: the unrolled stores of Poly_ScanConvertToSpanRegion (00076f54) before it end with a JMP at 000788dc and three zero bytes.

entries.name: Raster_FillContourTriangle
entries.description: (indices, points), callee-cleaned: fills the triangle of three int32 {x, y} points whose corners carry the three uint16 palette indices in contour bands. Two equal points draw nothing; with the highest and lowest index equal it fills the triangle with it (Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch(3), the index in the brush colour +4 at the clip block's (00098d64) +0x228). Otherwise it cuts the edge from the highest corner to the lowest at each whole index between them, and the two edges through the middle corner likewise, and fills each band between two cuts as a quadrilateral (Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch(4)) in the band's upper index, so a point takes the ceiling of its interpolated index; the corner order sets the quads' winding. ES2's Raster_FillContourTriangle (DBSIM 00486ddc).

entries.name: Raster_FillContourPolygon
entries.description: (count, points), callee-cleaned, entered also at its padding 0007965a-0007965b: brush mode 1 of Raster_DrawPolygonDispatch (00068be0), a polygon shaded per vertex. Sets the brush at the clip block's (00098d64) +0x228 to mode 0, maps each vertex's uint16 shade from the brush's list +0xc to a palette index through the ramp the brush colour's low word names (the 8-byte records at 0009a6f5: +0 the entry array, +4 the int16 length; entry (shade * length) >> 8), fans triangles from vertex 0 and fills each with Raster_FillContourTriangle (00078ccc); then puts back the brush colour +4 and mode 1. ES2's Raster_FillContourPolygon (DBSIM 004879c0).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 0007965c; es2_naming.py diff ES1DBSIM 0007965c DBSIM 004879c0

entries.name: TtmScript_Ctor
entries.description: (script): allocates the 0x1c1-byte .TTM script when given none (returning 0 when that fails); constructs twelve 0x18-byte objects at +0x58 with __vec_ctor; sets the dwords +0x19d and +0x1a5 to 0 and +0x1ad to 4, and zeroes +0x1b5, +0x1b9 and +0x1bd.

entries.name: GLRectangleRegion_Ctor
entries.description: (region): allocates 0x18 bytes when given none; stores the vtables 0009f25a, 0009f27e and 0009f2a6 in turn, runs the rect's and its points' inlined constructors at +8, then stores the vtable 0009f2ce and 0 at +4, the region type. ES1GO's GLRectangleRegion_Ctor (00046c6c) with the simulator's vtables. es2_xref finds its padding entry 0007987f stored at 000797db, in TtmScript_Ctor (000797ac), for the script's twelve regions.

entries.name: GLRectangleRegion_Dtor
entries.description: (region, flags): returns for none; otherwise stores the vtables 0009f2ce, 0009f2a6 and 0009f27e in turn and deletes the region when bit 0 of flags is set. ES1GO's GLRectangleRegion_Dtor (00046dc4) with the simulator's vtables. es2_xref finds it at 0009f2ea, the +0x1c slot of the vtable 0009f2ce.

entries.name: TtmScript_Dtor
entries.description: (script, flags): returns at once for a null script; otherwise calls TtmScript_Free (00079f68)(script) through its padding entry, destroys the twelve objects at +0x58 with __vec_dtor, and deletes the script when bit 0 of the flags is set.

entries.name: TtmScript_Run
entries.description: (script, ticks) in stack order, callee-cleaned: notes the default render context 0009f248 and, when the script's +0x1bd is not 0, sets 0009f248 to it and installs it with Raster_InstallRenderContext. Subtracts ticks from the wait word +0x182. While it is above 0: unless the mode dword +0xe is 2, runs the page byte +1 with TtmScript_RunPage (0007aa58). Otherwise: when the byte +0x18a is 1 subtracts ticks from +0x186 and, below 0, reloads it from +0x188 and calls TtmScript_CyclePalette (00079d90); reloads the wait from +0x184; then, for a mode of 3 or less by an unsigned test, through the table 0009f2f4: 0 runs the page, then takes the page +0x178 when it is not -1 (setting it to -1) or else adds 1 to the page and clears the byte +0x12, and when the page has reached the count byte +0 does as mode 3; 1 runs the page; 3, with the loop dword +0x13 1, resets the script with TtmScript_Reset (0007ca44) and sets the mode to 0, and otherwise sets the mode to 2 and leaves the script as it is; 2 goes to the end, as a mode above 3 does. Finally restores and installs the noted context and returns 1. es2_xref finds one call, from Ttm_RunAll (000695e0).

entries.name: TtmScript_BuildPath
entries.description: (script, name): rewrites the first .SCR in name to .DBM, .BMP to .DBA and .PAL to .DPL (Str_FindBoyerMoore, strncpy of 4), and returns the buffer 000bbbf0 holding the prefix 0009f254, when there is one, followed by the name. ES1GO's also upper-cases the name and rewrites .RAW.

entries.name: TtmScript_FixRect
entries.description: (script, rect): with the display object 0009f24c's +0x38 set to the low byte of its +0x3c and its +0x3c to 0009f250, Ttm_ManagerCtor's a (each store also copied to 00098dd6 or 00098dda and passed to the routine at 0009df14 or 0009df18 when the display is 000bdd28), copies a type-0 region of rect at (0, 0) with Region_CopyBetweenPages (00066914), passes rect to DirtyBox_Add (0008398c) with 0 (in stack order x0, y0, x1, y1, 0), then puts back the low bytes of the two fields. es2_xref finds calls from TtmScript_RunPage (0007aa58), three, and TtmScript_RunDrawCommand (0007c01c).

entries.name: TtmScript_CyclePalette
entries.description: (script): ES1GO's TtmScript_CyclePalette (000472d0) at the simulator's offsets: rotates by one place each of the three six-byte ranges at +0x18b whose direction (+0x18f, +0x195, +0x19b) is not 0 in the palette of the slot table +0x21 selected by +0x25, then uploads it with Palette_UploadWhole. es2_xref finds one call, from TtmScript_Run (00079a14).

entries.name: TtmScript_FindLabel
entries.description: (script, label): the first page, in page order below the count byte +0, whose first command in the page table +2 is 0x1101 or 0x1111 with label as its argument, as a byte; 0 when none is. ES1GO's TtmScript_FindLabel (0004741a) also formats a message.

entries.name: TtmScript_Free
entries.description: (script): resets the script with TtmScript_Reset (0007ca44) through its padding entry, then deletes the unpacked script +6, the page table +2 and the slot tables +0x21 and +0x17 when set. ES1GO's TtmScript_Free (000474bd) also destroys a sound object. es2_xref finds one call, from TtmScript_Dtor, through the padding entry 00079f67.

entries.name: TtmScript_SkipString
entries.description: (script, string): returns the address past the string's NUL, plus one more byte when the string's length is even, so the next opcode word starts on an even offset.

entries.name: TtmScript_CopyArgBytes
entries.description: (script, source, count): copies count bytes from source, or with a count of 0 the bytes up to its NUL, at most 100 either way, into the buffer 000bbc18, adds a NUL and returns the buffer. ES1GO's TtmScript_CopyArgBytes (0004759d) with the simulator's buffer.

entries.name: Ttm_TokenName
entries.description: (ignored, opcode) in stack order, callee-cleaned: Dynamix's name of a .TTM opcode: searches the 128 opcodes at 0009fb14 and jumps (0007a06d) through the table 0009fd14 to a case returning its string, or returns unknown (0009fb0c). The opcodes and the 2,034 bytes of strings from 0009f322 are the same as ES1GO's Ttm_TokenName (00047618)'s. es2_xref finds no reference to it.

entries.name: TtmScript_Load
entries.description: (script, a, b, name) in stack order, callee-cleaned: loads a .TTM. Opens TtmScript_BuildPath (00079b54)'s path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath and returns 3 when its status is not 0; TtmScript_FindTag (0007cba4) PAG:, reads the size dword and one byte, the page count's low byte; TT3:, reads the size dword and the method byte, returning 2 unless it is 1, then the unpacked length; allocates it at +6 (1 when that fails) and reads it through an RLERStream on the file stream, returning 1 when the file stream's status is then not 0. Closes the file stream, stores the page count byte at +0, count + 1 dwords at +2, +6 + length - 1 at +0xa, 0x18 bytes at +0x21 and +0x17, freeing them and returning 1 when one fails; indexes the pages with TtmScript_IndexPages (0007a940) through its padding entry; zeroes the two blocks and the fields, stores a at +0xe and b at +0x13, 0xff at the bytes +0x178 and +0x179, 10 at the dwords +0x1a1, +0x1a9 and +0x1b1; destroys the streams (RLERStream_DtorCopy (0007a914)'s vtable 0009ff16, VolRStream_Dtor) and returns the index result, 0 or 2. ES1GO's TtmScript_Load does not test the open or the method byte and reads the page count as a word. es2_xref finds one call, from Ttm_Open.

entries.name: RLERStream_DtorCopy
entries.description: (stream, flags): RLERStream_Dtor's code with the TTM module's copy of RLERStream's vtable, 0009ff16: returns at once for a null stream; otherwise stores that vtable, Stream_BaseDtor(stream, 0), and Mem_Delete when bit 0 of the flags is set.

entries.name: TtmScript_IndexPages
entries.description: (script): ES1GO's TtmScript_IndexPages over this script's fields (page count byte +0, page table +2, script +6, last byte +0xa): stores each page's start and steps over commands to the step past an opcode 0x0ff0, returning 2 when the position reaches +0xa at a page's start or after a command, or on low bits 8-14, and 0 with every page found. Strings are skipped with TtmScript_SkipString (00079fb0).

entries.name: TtmScript_RunPage
entries.description: (script, page) in stack order, callee-cleaned: ES1GO's TtmScript_RunPage (00048218) at the simulator's offsets, running the page from the page table +2 to its 0x0ff0 and returning 1, with these differences. Its call offsets (depth +0x17a, x +0x17c, y +0x17e) skip the opcodes of the table 0009ffac (targets 0009ffbc, JMP 0007ad1d). It steps over every opcode 0xc000-0xcfff; hands 0xa000-0xafff to TtmScript_RunDrawCommand (0007c01c), returning 0 when that returns 0; finds the rest in the 29 opcodes at 0009ffcc (targets 000a0040, JMP 0007adea), the shell's 30 less 0x5005, and steps over any other. Point lists go through TtmScript_CopyArgBytes (00079fdc). Loads, frees, palette selects, 0x0020, 0x4204, 0x4214, 0x2402, 0x0400, 0xf01f and 0x4124 act while the wait +0x182 is 0 or less; 0x1021 and 0x2022 act once per page through the byte +0x12, 0x2022 as min + labs(rand (0007cd28)() % (max - min)); 0x4114 acts on every run. Palettes are uploaded with Palette_UploadWhole on select and load; bitmap arrays are destroyed with GLBitmapArray_Dtor (000673c8)(array, 3); 0xf01f's bitmap is loaded with ClassItem_LoadResource and its rect fixed with TtmScript_FixRect (00079c38). The fades work on a stack palette set up with GLPalette_Assign (0007bfdc), scale colours a1 to a2 toward black with Palette_ScaleRange (0007cc24) by the step 6 - a4, copy the full screen with Region_CopyBetweenPages (00066914) and destroy the copy with GLPalette_Dtor (00069258). Labels are found with TtmScript_FindLabel (00079ef4). es2_xref finds calls from TtmScript_Run (00079a14), three, and from its own 0x3003 and 0x3303 cases, through the padding entry 0007aa57.

entries.name: GLPalette_Assign
entries.description: (palette, source): copies the words +4, +6, +0xc, +0xe and the dwords +8 (the colours) and +0x10 from source, leaving the vtable. ES1GO's GLPalette_Assign (0004a08c). es2_xref finds calls from the two fade cases of TtmScript_RunPage (0007aa58).

entries.name: TtmScript_RunDrawCommand
entries.description: (script, string, seven arguments, opcode) in stack order, callee-cleaned: ES1GO's TtmScript_RunDrawCommand (0004a213) at the simulator's offsets: matches the opcode against the shell's 22 at 000a00b4 (targets 000a010c, JMP 0007c040) and returns 1 whether or not one matches. The pen +0x228 and fill +0x22c of the default render context 0009f248 are set to the brushes +0x19d, +0x1a5 and +0x1ad. Each draw but 0xa601 passes its box to DirtyBox_Add (0008398c) with 1; the ellipses draw with Raster_DrawEllipse (000831f4) and the sized brush with Bitmap_BlitScaled (00067178); one case serves the twelve bitmap draws, testing the opcode's low four bits, and adds the dwords +0x1b5 and +0x1b9 to the position. 0xa601, while the wait +0x182 is 0 or less, puts the selected region's saved pixels back with Region_Restore at (0, 0) and passes the region's rect to TtmScript_FixRect (00079c38). es2_xref finds one call, from TtmScript_RunPage (0007aa58), through the padding entry 0007c01b.

entries.name: Point_DefaultCtor
entries.description: (point): allocates 8 bytes when given none and returns the point as it was. ES1GO's Point_DefaultCtor (0004b37d). es2_xref finds its padding entry 0007ca25 stored at 0007c46f, in the polygon case of TtmScript_RunDrawCommand (0007c01c), which passes it to __vec_new.

entries.name: TtmScript_Reset
entries.description: (script): destroys the six palettes of the slot table +0x21 through their +0x1c slot with 3 and the six bitmap arrays of +0x17 with GLBitmapArray_Dtor (000673c8)(array, 3), deletes the twelve saved-pixel buffers at +0x28, zeroing every slot; zeroes the cycling directions +0x18f, +0x195 and +0x19b; sets the mode dword +0xe to 2, the page byte +1 and the palette slot +0x25 to 0, the word +0x178 to -1, the words +0x17a to +0x188 and the byte +0x18a to 0, and the brush colours +0x1a1, +0x1a9 and +0x1b1 to 10. ES1GO's TtmScript_Reset (0004b3c6) at the simulator's offsets; this one leaves the byte +0x12. es2_xref finds calls from TtmScript_Run (00079a14), two, and TtmScript_Free (00079f68), through the padding entry 0007ca43.

entries.name: TtmScript_FindTag
entries.description: (script, tag, stream): ES1GO's Stream_FindTag search with the script first, unused: notes the stream's position (slot +8) and reads a byte at a time (slot +0x1c) until the NUL-terminated tag has matched or a read fails; a matching byte advances through the tag, a byte that does not match restarts at the tag's first byte without being tested against it; on a failure seeks (slot +0xc) back. Returns whether the whole tag matched, the stream then just past it.

entries.name: Palette_ScaleRange
entries.description: (script, percent, last, first, source, target): for each colour from first to last inclusive, sets target's colour to source's with each of the three channels multiplied by Math_Q10Multiply by (percent << 10) / 100, and the fourth byte 1. The simulator's fades use it where ES1GO's use Palette_BlendRange (0004b532), which blends toward a colour. es2_xref finds two calls, from the fade cases of TtmScript_RunPage (0007aa58).

entries.name: rand
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `rand`, from `rand.c`: Symantec C++ 6.1's library code for it matches here whole, relocated operands masked, and the search over the image finds it at this address only. The match covers 34 bytes from here. Sets the state 000a0164 to state x 0x41c64e6d + 0x3039 and returns its bits 16 to 30; srand (0007cd4a) sets the state.

entries.name: srand
entries.description: (seed), C convention: stores seed at 000a0164, the state rand (0007cd28) steps. es2_xref finds one call, from Ttm_ManagerCtor (00069540), which passes clock().

entries.name: clock
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `clock`, from `clock.ASM`: Symantec C++ 6.1's library code for it matches here whole, relocated operands masked, and the search over the image finds it at this address only. The match covers 60 bytes from here.

entries.description: The code of ES1GO's GLFont_GetStreamSize (000666ec), relocated operands aside; slot +0x08 of the vtable 000a01ba.

entries.name: GLFont_GetMemorySize
entries.description: The code of ES1GO's GLFont_GetMemorySize (0006673c), relocated operands aside; slot +0x0c of the vtable 000a01ba.

entries.name: GLFont_WriteToStream
entries.description: The code of ES1GO's GLFont_WriteToStream (0006678c), relocated operands aside; slot +0x14 of the vtable 000a01ba.

entries.name: GLFont_ReadFromStream
entries.description: The code of ES1GO's GLFont_ReadFromStream (00066978), relocated operands aside; slot +0x10 of the vtable 000a01ba.

entries.name: Line_ScanConvertToSpanRegion
entries.description: (a, b, out), C convention: writes the int16 span region of a one-pixel line between the int32 points a and b: the top row min(y), the row count |dy| + 1, then an {x0, x1} pair per row from the top. A single point is one row {x, x}; a horizontal line one row {min x, max x}; a vertical line {x, x} on each row; any other the run of x a Bresenham walk from the smaller-x end puts on each row, its error starting at 2dy - dx for a shallow line and 2dx - dy for a steep one, the rows written from the last back when y falls along the walk. es2_xref finds three calls, all from Raster_DrawLine (0006a064). ES2's Line_ScanConvertToSpanRegion (DBSIM 00483c60), the same statements.
entries.source: Herculan/docs/es1/rendering/screen-pages.md#lines-and-clipped-bitmaps; ES1DBSIM decompile at 0007d358, against ES2's Line_ScanConvertToSpanRegion

entries.name: Line_ClipToRect
entries.description: (a, b, rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}), C convention: cuts the segment between the int32 points a and b, in place, to the inclusive rect, taking y0, x0, y1 and x1 in that order. When both endpoints lie beyond a bound it returns 0, leaving both points as they were; when one does, that endpoint moves onto the bound at the crossing computed from it toward the other (IMUL, then IDIV of the 64-bit product, the quotient truncated toward zero). To move b it first exchanges the two points (XCHG) and leaves them exchanged, so the result can hold the endpoints in the other order. Stores both points and returns 1. A point on a bound is inside. ES2's Line_ClipToRect (DBSIM 00483b60), identical after normalisation. An object file of its own, between the zero fills after the RETs at 0007d4a2 and 0007d5a1. es2_xref finds three calls, from Raster_DrawLine (0006a064).
entries.source: ES1DBSIM disassembly at 0007d4a4, against ES2's Line_ClipToRect

entries.name: toupper
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime `toupper`, from `is.c`: Symantec C++ 6.1's library code for it matches here whole, relocated operands masked, and the search over the image finds it at this address only. The match covers 24 bytes from here.

entries.name: GL_ClaimGlobal
entries.description: (this, instance, index) in stack order, callee-cleaned: allocates 4 bytes for a null this, clears +0, and stores instance in GL slot index (000bdd0c + index * 4) when the slot is empty. ES2's GL_ClaimGlobal (DBSIM 00480484). GLDisplay_Ctor passes slot 7, the current display.

entries.name: GL_SetGlobal
entries.description: (value, index) in stack order, callee-cleaned: returns 1 and stores nothing when value is non-null and GL slot index (000bdd0c + index * 4) already holds one; otherwise stores value there and returns 0. ES2's GL_SetGlobal (DBSIM 004804a8), its arguments reversed.

entries.name: atexit
entries.description: Symantec C++ runtime atexit: (function): points _atexitp (000bdabe) at 000bdac2 on first use, and while the list has room (the pointer at most 000bdb41) advances it by 4 and stores the function there, returning 0; returns 1 when the list is full.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitTransparent
entries.description: (bitmap, point, flags), callee-cleaned: the draw of a type-1 bitmap for Raster_BlitDispatch (0006a8e0), its int16 rows +0 and columns +2 and its data +0xa, a 16-byte colour table followed by a code stream. Returns when the bitmap misses the clip block's (00098d64) rect +0x20c to +0x218; flags bit 0 draws it upside down (rows from the bottom up) and bit 1 mirrored (columns from the right). Codes: bit 7 set is a run of code & 0x3f pixels, cut to the rect's columns and drawn only while its row is within the rect's rows: with bit 6 clear one colour, the colour-table entry the following byte names, through slot 24 (0009df34) or, in clip mode +0x204 2, slot 25 (0009df38); with bit 6 set (count + 1) / 2 bytes of 4-bit colour-table indices, high nibble first, through slot 22 (0009df2c) or 23 (0009df30). 0x40 ends the bitmap; 0x41 to 0x7f skip that many transparent pixels; 0x01 to 0x3f end a row, taking x back by the code, or by 64 times the following byte plus the code when that byte is 0x01 to 0x3f. Saves the pen's +4 (+0x224) and puts it back. ES2's Bitmap_BlitTransparent (DBSIM 00488cec).

entries.name: GLCursor_Construct
entries.description: (mode, stream) in stack order, callee-cleaned: the load function the GL class table (0009f198) registers for tag 0x28000b 'GLCursor': 0x10 bytes from the current arena (Arena_Alloc on 000bd954), GLCursor_Ctor (0006b348), then the cursor's read slot +0x10 with its two arguments. DBSIM's GLCursor_Construct (00483268), whose read slot is +0xc.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 0007dc68 and the class table at 0009f1f0; the same statements as ES1GO 000663b0 (es2_naming diff)

entries.name: GLCursor_GetClassTag
entries.description: Returns 0x28000b, callee-cleaned (RET 4): slot +4 of the GLCursor vtable 0009b672.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM image bytes at 0007dca0 (b8 0b 00 28 00 c2 04 00) and the vtable at 0009b672

entries.name: GLCursor_GetStreamSize
entries.description: (cursor), callee-cleaned: slot +8 of the GLCursor vtable: ClassItem_ItemTotalSize of the bitmap +4 plus 8 for the hotspot, or 0 when that size is 0.
entries.source: ES1DBSIM decompile at 0007dca8; the same statements as ES1GO 000663f0 (es2_naming diff)

entries.name: GLCursor_GetMemorySize

entries.name: GLCursor_ReadFromStream
entries.description: (cursor, mode, stream) in stack order, callee-cleaned: slot +0x10 of the GLCursor vtable: reads 8 bytes, the hotspot's x and y, into +8 through the stream's slot +0x1c, then one class item, the bitmap, into +4 with ClassItem_LoadResource(0, stream). DBSIM's GLCursor_ReadFromStream (00483320) at slot +0xc.

entries.name: GLCursor_WriteToStream
entries.description: (cursor, mode, stream) in stack order, callee-cleaned: slot +0x14 of the GLCursor vtable: writes the 8 hotspot bytes at +8 through the stream's slot +0x18, then the bitmap +4 with ClassItem_StoreItem(bitmap, 0, stream).

entries.name: Keyboard_Int15Handler
entries.description: Interrupt 0x15 handler: for AH other than 0x4f jumps to the saved vector at 0009b69c. For 0x4f, saves the registers, loads DS from 0009b6a6, switches to the stack 000a11e0 (SS from 0009b6a8), and with AL 0xe0 adds 2 to Keyboard_PrefixCount (0009b6b0); otherwise passes AL to Keyboard_Dispatch (0007de20). Then halves the count and returns with the carry set (the BIOS processes the key) for an E0 byte or a dispatch answer of 0; for a non-zero answer it returns with the carry clear, or with AL 0xe0 and the carry set when the count's halving shifted out a 1. No Ghidra function.

entries.name: Keyboard_Int9Handler
entries.description: Interrupt 9 handler: saves the registers, loads DS from 0009b6a6, switches to the stack 000a11e0 (SS from 0009b6a8), reads one byte from port 0x60 into EAX (upper bits 0), calls Keyboard_Dispatch (0007de20), sends 0x20 to port 0x20, restores and returns with IRETD, not passing the interrupt to the saved vector. No Ghidra function.

entries.name: Keyboard_Dispatch
entries.description: The byte in EAX. With Keyboard_TranslateTable (0009b7ba) set, replaces the low seven bits by its entry, keeping bit 0x80. Sets bit 0x8000 of Keyboard_Modifiers (0009b6ae) while Keyboard_PrefixCount (0009b6b0) is not 0 and clears it otherwise; ors the modifiers' high byte into the code. By the byte's low seven bits: 0x2a and 0x36 set (press) or clear (release) modifier bits 2 and 1, 0x3a flips 0x40 on a press, and after those three 0x800 = (bit 1 or bit 2) xor bit 0x40; 0x38 sets or clears 0x200, 0x1d 0x400; 0x45 flips 0x1000 and 0x46 0x2000 on a press. entries.name: HmiMidi_SongTick
entries.description: Far timer handler of the HMI library, for the song in the byte 0009d910: returns unless the playing flag 000a22ac is set and the paused flag 000a226c clear. With a fade count 000a7820, on every fourth call (the byte 000a7840) it takes 1 off the count, moves the 16.16 volume 000a7800 by the step 000a77e0 (down for flags 2 and 4, up for 1) and calls HmiMidi_SetSongVolume (0006f64e); flag 4 at a count of 0 ends the song. Then for each track below the count 000a2198 it adds 1 to the tick count 000a1d48 and, while the events pointer 000a1348 is set and the count has reached the delta 000a1948, handles the event: its length from the table 000a22cc by the status's high nibble or 000a22dc by the low nibble of a status of 0xf0 or more; 0xff 0x2f clears the track's pointer and takes 1 off 000a2178, ending the song at 0, else length 3; 0xff 0x51 is length 5; other 0xff events and controllers 0x6c, 0x6e, 0x71, 0x74, 0x78 are stepped over; 0x6d and 0x73 copy the byte 6 past the status into the loop count +6 of the track's branch entry of the event's value; 0x6f/0x70 (every track from 1 with a pointer) and 0x75/0x76 (this track) take 1 off that count unless 0 or 0xff, call the loop callback 000a5fbc with (song, track, id, count) and branch while the count and the answer are non-zero; 0x72 (every track from 1) and 0x79 (this track) call the branch callback 000a5f8c with (song, track, id | 0x80) and branch to that id unless it answers 0; 0x77 calls the trigger callback of the value; any other event goes to HmiMidi_SendEvent (000715c5) with the track's driver slot. A branch sets the pointer to the chunk + the entry's +0 + 0xc, sends a program change with the entry's +5 and the entry's data pairs as controllers, and leaves the pointer there. After an event the tick count is zeroed, the pointer moves by the length and past the next delta, read by HmiMidi_ReadDelta (0006ed60), and the loop goes on while that delta is 0. Ending the song: clears the playing flag, HmiMidi_SilenceSong (00071f84), HmiTimer_RemoveEvent (0006d8d5), HmiMidi_ResetSong (0006eb98), then a far call of the callback at the file's +0x300 with the song.

entries.description: (device, slot, address out, far pointer out, far pointer out, allocation out) of the HMI library: 10 for a slot above 5, 9 when the slot's flag 000a12e4 is set, 6 for a device outside 0xa000-0xa200. Copies the path at 000a575c to 000a585c, appends hmimdrv.386 and opens it, 0xf on failure; reads the 0x2c-byte header to 000a2514, then 0x30-byte entry headers to 000a2540 while the index is at most the count +0x20 and no entry matched, seeking past an image by its size +0x24 when its device +0x28 differs. For the match: malloc of the size + 0x1068 (5 on failure), the address rounded up to 4 KB, two selectors from maybe_X32_AllocSelector, the second given the code segment's rights by 0008076c, the image read to the address and locked with X32_LockRegion. entries.name: HmiDigiMidi_SendEvent
entries.description: (far event, length, slot), device 0xa005's send, a far function; it answers 0 and reads the event's status, its channel the low four bits, the note or controller byte 1 and the value byte 2. A note on with a velocity, for a note whose far pointer HmiDigiMidi_NoteSamples (000a3048)[slot][note] is not null: unless the start block's +0x24 is 0xffff8000, stops the voice HmiDigiMidi_TakeNoteVoice (0008229d)(slot, note, channel) takes with HmiDigi_StopSample (0006dd7f) on the slot's digital driver HmiDigiMidi_DigiDriver (000a3f68); when HmiDigiMidi_VoiceCount (000a3014) has reached HmiDigiMidi_VoiceLimit (000a3000), stops the voice HmiDigiMidi_TakeChannelVoice (000821a7)(slot, channel) takes; with HmiDigiMidi_UseVelocity (000a3fb8) set, writes ((the slot's volume HmiDigiMidi_SlotLevels (000a259c) +0 * velocity) >> 7) << 8 to the block's +0x14; writes the note to +0x18 and, with bit 0x80 of the slot's pan (+4) clear, the pan << 9 to +0x40; starts the block with HmiDigi_StartSample (0006dad9) and, given a voice, records it with HmiDigiMidi_AddVoice (0008212c)(slot, voice, note, velocity, channel). A note on with velocity 0, and a note off, stop the note's voice under the same +0x24 test. Controller 0x7b stops every voice HmiDigiMidi_TakeChannelVoice takes for the channel; controller 7 stores the value as the slot's volume and passes value * the voice's velocity * 2 to HmiDigi_SetSampleVolume (0006e0b3) for each recorded voice from HmiDigiMidi_VoiceOldest (000a2fec) to HmiDigiMidi_VoiceNext (000a2fd8); controller 10 stores the value as the slot's pan and passes value << 9 to HmiDigi_SetSamplePan (0006e265) for each. Any other event does nothing.

entries.name: HmiDigiMidi_Open
entries.description: (far block, slot, x), device 0xa005's open, a far function. With a digital driver whose entry at 000a231c + driver * 0x5c has +0x14 equal to the block's device +0x00, among the first five, takes its number and clears HmiDigiMidi_OwnsDriver (000a3fa4)[slot]. Otherwise sets it, opens the device with HmiDigi_InitDriver (0006fe3a)(block +0x00, far block +0x1c, far block +0x14, far handle), answering its error, and registers the far handler the open left at the init block's +0x1c with HmiTimer_AddEvent (0006d5e6) at the block's +0x04 calls a second, keeping the event number at HmiDigiMidi_TimerEvent (000a3f90)[slot] and setting HmiDigiMidi_TimerAdded (000a3f7c)[slot], answering its error. Then stores the driver at HmiDigiMidi_DigiDriver (000a3f68)[slot], the block's +0x10 at HmiDigiMidi_UseVelocity (000a3fb8)[slot] and the slot at HmiDigiMidi_DriverSlot (000a7848)[driver], calls HmiDigiMidi_ClearVoices (000820c5)(slot, block +0x0c), sets bit 0x80 of the pan of all five slots of HmiDigiMidi_SlotLevels (000a259c), and answers 0.

entries.description: (far pointer, slot, x), device 0xa005's close, a far function: with HmiDigiMidi_TimerAdded (000a3f7c)[slot] set, clears it and, with HmiDigiMidi_OwnsDriver (000a3fa4)[slot] set, closes the driver with HmiDigi_UninitDriver (000705c5)(HmiDigiMidi_DigiDriver (000a3f68)[slot], 1, 1) and removes the timer event HmiDigiMidi_TimerEvent (000a3f90)[slot] with HmiTimer_RemoveEvent (0006d8d5); then calls HmiDigiMidi_CloseNoOp (00082127)(slot) and answers 0. HmiMidi_CloseDriver (0007144b) passes HmiMidi_DriverArg (000a5984) where it reads the slot.

entries.description: (far pointer, slot, x), device 0xa005's reset, a far function: HmiDigiMidi_ClearVoices (000820c5)(slot, HmiDigiMidi_VoiceLimit (000a3000)[slot]), forgetting the slot's recorded voices without stopping them, and answers 0.

entries.description: (far bank, slot, x), device 0xa005's bank function, a far function: keeps the bank's far pointer at HmiDigiMidi_Banks (000a3f48)[slot], clears the slot's 128 far pointers of HmiDigiMidi_NoteSamples (000a3048), and answers 0xe unless the bank opens with HmiDigiMidi_BankSignature (000a3fcc), HMIDIGIP. From offset 0x28, while the offset is below the bank's dword +0x24, each entry is a 0x74-byte start block and its data: the note entry of the block's +0x18 gets a far pointer to the block, the block's +0x00 a far pointer to its data at +0x74, its +0x1c the far callback HmiDigiMidi_SampleCallback (00081e1d), and the next entry starts the block's +0x08 + 0x74 on. entries.name: LZHuffman_Ctor
entries.description: LZHuffman constructor, callee-cleaned (this): allocates 0x16 bytes through Mem_New when this is null (0 if that fails), then through Mem_New the frequency table +4 (0x4e8 bytes), the parent links +8 (0x75a) and the child links +0xc (0x4e6), LZHUF's sizes for 314 symbols and a 627-node tree. The class stores no vptr. ES2's LZHuffman_Ctor (DBSIM 0047bb50).

entries.name: LZHuffman_Dtor
entries.description: LZHuffman destructor (this, flags): returns at once for a null this; otherwise Mem_Delete on the tables +4, +8 and +0xc, and on this when bit 0 of the flags is set. ES2's LZHuffman_Dtor (DBSIM 0047bb90).

entries.name: LZHuffman_Start
entries.description: (coder, source): attaches the source at +0, clears the bit-input state +0x10..+0x15, and builds LZHUF's initial tree: 314 (0x13a) leaves of frequency 1 (frequencies +4) whose child links (+0xc) are 0x273 + i and parent links (+8, from +0x4e6) their node, then the internal nodes 0x13a..0x272 each summing a pair, the sentinel frequency 0xffff at node 0x273 and parent 0 for the root 0x272. LZHUF's StartHuff. ES2's LZHuffman_Start (DBSIM 0047bbd0).

entries.name: LZHuffman_EncodeChar
entries.description: (coder, c): walks the parent links (+8, leaf c's at +0x4e6) up to the root 0x272, shifting each node's low bit into the code from the top, then LZHuffman_PutCode(coder, code, bit count) and LZHuffman_Update(coder, c). LZHUF's EncodeChar. ES2's LZHuffman_EncodeChar (DBSIM 0047bc80).

entries.name: LZHuffman_EncodePosition
entries.description: (coder, position): LZHuffman_PutCode with the code 000a7cd0[position >> 6] << 8 and the length 000a7c90[position >> 6] (LZHUF's p_code and p_len), then the low six bits << 10 in 6 bits. LZHUF's EncodePosition. ES2's LZHuffman_EncodePosition (DBSIM 0047bcd4).

entries.name: LZHuffman_DecodeChar
entries.description: (coder): walks the child links (+0xc) from the root (+0x4e4) one LZHuffman_GetBit at a time until a leaf (>= 0x273), LZHuffman_Update's it and returns leaf - 0x273. LZHUF's DecodeChar. ES2's LZHuffman_DecodeChar (DBSIM 0047bd18).

entries.name: LZHuffman_DecodePosition
entries.description: (coder): reads a byte with LZHuffman_GetByte, takes the upper six bits from 000a7d10 and the bit count from 000a7e10 (LZHUF's d_code and d_len), shifts count - 2 more bits from LZHuffman_GetBit into the byte from below and returns its low six bits | upper << 6, a 12-bit position. LZHUF's DecodePosition. ES2's LZHuffman_DecodePosition (DBSIM 0047bd68).

entries.name: LZHuffman_EncodeEnd
entries.description: (coder): writes the top byte of the bit buffer (+0x13) when bits are pending (+0x15), then a zero byte, each through the stream's slot +0x18. LZHUF's EncodeEnd with a trailing 0. ES2's LZHuffman_EncodeEnd (DBSIM 0047bdbc).

entries.name: LZHuffman_GetBit
entries.description: (coder): while the bit count +0x12 is below 9, reads a byte through the source's slot +0x1c (0 when the read fails), ORs it into the 16-bit buffer +0x10 below the bits held and adds 8 to the count; then shifts out and returns the top bit. LZHUF's GetBit. ES2's LZHuffman_GetBit (DBSIM 0047bdec).

entries.name: LZHuffman_GetByte
entries.description: (coder): LZHuffman_GetBit's refill, then shifts out and returns the top 8 bits. LZHUF's GetByte. ES2's LZHuffman_GetByte (DBSIM 0047be4c).

entries.name: LZHuffman_PutCode
entries.description: (coder, code, length) in stack order: ORs the code, shifted right by the pending bit count +0x15, into the output buffer +0x13 and adds length to the count; at 8 bits or more writes the buffer's top byte through the stream's slot +0x18, and when 8 still remain its low byte too and keeps code << (length - count). LZHUF's Putcode. ES2's LZHuffman_PutCode (DBSIM 0047beac).

entries.name: LZHuffman_Reconstruct
entries.description: (coder): rebuilds the adaptive Huffman tree: gathers the leaves (child link above 0x272) to the front with their frequencies (+4) halved, rounding up, rebuilds the internal nodes 0x13a..0x272 in frequency order with memmove, and relinks the parents (+8). LZHUF's reconst. ES2's LZHuffman_Reconstruct (DBSIM 0047bf20).

entries.name: LZHuffman_Update
entries.description: (coder, c): LZHuffman_Reconstruct when the root frequency (+4 at 0x4e4) is 0x8000, then increments the frequencies from leaf c up to the root, swapping a node past its lower-frequency successors to keep the order, with their child and parent links. LZHUF's update. ES2's LZHuffman_Update (DBSIM 0047c054).

entries.name: flushall
entries.description: The runtime's flushall, C convention: fflush on every FILE of _iob up to 0009eb4c that is open (flags +0xc & 0x83), returning how many it flushed.

entries.description: (delay, height, width, y, x) in stack order, callee-cleaned: ES1GO's DirtyBox_Add in other code, measuring the display 000bdd28 with GLDisplay_GetAttribute (0006a780) and taking its record from DirtyBox_Alloc (000838e4) for DirtyList_Insert (00083bb4).
